epics.title: E00 — Project Foundation
epics.description:
## Outcome
A trustworthy engineering foundation: every change lands through a green, coverage-gated, security-scanned PR; the sim core is deterministic and replayable; content is schema-validated; a greybox testbed boots in the chosen engine; and a public backlog.html always shows what is done and what is next.
## Scope
- In: Repo scaffold (TS strict, Vite, pnpm), lint/format/typecheck, Vitest + Playwright
- In: CI pipeline with per-layer coverage thresholds, ratchet, determinism lint, secret scanning, dependency CVE gate
- In: Branch protection, PR template with Closes lines, CHANGELOG, coverage-exclusions.md process
- In: backlog.html generator + GitHub Pages deploy
- In: Engine ADR spike (Three.js vs Babylon.js incl. physics/Rapier)
- In: Deterministic sim core, state hashing, replay harness, content pipeline, greybox testbed
- Out: Gameplay systems (E02+)
- Out: Save/load (mw-e30)
- Out: Perf budget suite beyond the baseline scene (mw-e32)
- Out: Debug console and content tools (mw-e33)
## Exit criteria
- A PR that lowers coverage, calls Math.random in src/sim, leaks a secret, or adds a CRITICAL CVE dependency is blocked by required checks.
- backlog.html on GitHub Pages reflects a merged PR's Closes lines within one workflow run of the merge.
- ADR-0001 records the engine + physics choice with measured evidence from the reference machine.
- The greybox testbed boots in Chrome, Firefox and Safari with zero console errors and a replay test reproduces identical sim state hashes.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 A PR that lowers coverage, calls Math.random in src/sim, leaks a secret, or adds a CRITICAL CVE dependency is blocked by required checks.
- EC-2 backlog.html on GitHub Pages reflects a merged PR's Closes lines within one workflow run of the merge.
- EC-3 ADR-0001 records the engine + physics choice with measured evidence from the reference machine.
- EC-4 The greybox testbed boots in Chrome, Firefox and Safari with zero console errors and a replay test reproduces identical sim state hashes.

epics.title: E30 — Save/Load
epics.description:
## Outcome
Browser-safe saves reliably preserve character and world state across sessions, browser restarts and game updates; a corrupted or interrupted save never costs the player all their progress.
## Scope
- In: Versioned save envelope, sim-state serialization via a section registry, migrations
- In: IndexedDB storage with fallback, slots, autosave, quicksave, death→reload flow
- In: Corruption recovery, multi-tab guard, export/import, save/load UI
- Out: Cloud saves / accounts (post-MVP, not planned)
- Out: World-fact modelling itself (see e27-world-state-store)
## Exit criteria
- Every save schema change ships with a migration and a committed fixture that CI loads successfully.
- Killing the tab mid-write never leaves zero loadable saves (automated test).
- Save/load code paths have 100% coverage.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 Every save schema change ships with a migration and a committed fixture that CI loads successfully.
- EC-2 Killing the tab mid-write never leaves zero loadable saves (automated test).
- EC-3 Save/load code paths have 100% coverage.

epics.title: E31 — Accessibility & Settings
epics.description:
## Outcome
Players can tailor controls, text, camera, audio, visuals and difficulty so the game is comfortable and playable for a broad audience, meeting the basic tier of the Game Accessibility Guidelines.
## Scope
- In: Settings framework and options UI
- In: Remapping, hold/toggle, text scaling, captions for gameplay-critical sounds, camera and motion comfort, colour-blind support, difficulty assists, menu keyboard/gamepad navigation
- In: Accessibility audit
- Out: Graphics quality presets implementation (see e32-quality-presets)
- Out: Voice/TTS narration (no voice in MVP)
## Exit criteria
- Every setting persists across reloads and applies without restarting the game.
- All menus are fully operable by keyboard only and by gamepad only (automated e2e).
- Accessibility audit against GAG basic tier has no open P1 findings.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 Every setting persists across reloads and applies without restarting the game.
- EC-2 All menus are fully operable by keyboard only and by gamepad only (automated e2e).
- EC-3 Accessibility audit against GAG basic tier has no open P1 findings.

epics.title: E32 — Performance & Browser Compatibility
epics.description:
## Outcome
Stable frame pacing and fast loading on the hardware baseline across current desktop Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, protected by automated budgets so regressions are caught in PRs rather than playtests.
## Scope
- In: Perf budget suite, bundle/sim-tick budgets, browser matrix, capability detection, quality presets + dynamic resolution, asset loading/caching, context-loss recovery, memory-leak tests, reference-machine runbook
- Out: Mobile performance profiles (mw-e36)
- Out: Engine selection (e00-engine-decision)
## Exit criteria
- High preset holds 60 fps (p95 frame time ≤ 16.7 ms) in the combat stress scene on the reference machine.
- Initial load to playable ≤ 10 s at 50 Mbps, warm reload ≤ 3 s, initial download ≤ 50 MB, JS heap ≤ 1.5 GB.
- Smoke suite green on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit in CI.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 High preset holds 60 fps (p95 frame time ≤ 16.7 ms) in the combat stress scene on the reference machine.
- EC-2 Initial load to playable ≤ 10 s at 50 Mbps, warm reload ≤ 3 s, initial download ≤ 50 MB, JS heap ≤ 1.5 GB.
- EC-3 Smoke suite green on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit in CI.

epics.title: E33 — Developer/Content Tools
epics.description:
## Outcome
Developers and designers can create, tune and debug spells, creatures, loot, encounters, dialogue and puzzles in minutes, with visual insight into the systemic simulation and one-keypress bug capture.
## Scope
- In: Debug console + cheats, entity inspector, time controls, overlays (AI, world systems), sandboxes (spells, creatures), content validator/scaffolder/hot reload, dialogue/quest/loot tooling, replay bug capture
- Out: Full level editor (use external DCC/greybox kit)
- Out: Player-facing modding
## Exit criteria
- Adding a new spell/creature/item from scaffold to in-game test takes ≤ 10 minutes without restarting the dev server.
- All dev tools are stripped from production builds (bundle check).
- A captured bug report replays deterministically on another machine.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 Adding a new spell/creature/item from scaffold to in-game test takes ≤ 10 minutes without restarting the dev server.
- EC-2 All dev tools are stripped from production builds (bundle check).
- EC-3 A captured bug report replays deterministically on another machine.

epics.title: E34 — Telemetry & Playtesting
epics.description:
## Outcome
Privacy-first, local-first, opt-in measurement of deaths, abandoned encounters, spell usage, puzzle completion and other signals that complements — never replaces — direct observation of players.
## Scope
- In: Event schema + local store + export
- In: Consent/opt-in, gameplay events, error capture, in-game feedback, playtest bundle export, analysis scripts, optional opt-in upload
- Out: Third-party analytics SDKs, fingerprinting, ads (never)
- Out: Running the playtests (mw-e35)
## Exit criteria
- With default settings the game makes zero telemetry network requests (automated e2e).
- A playtester can export one bundle file and an analysis script turns N bundles into a death heatmap + spell/puzzle report.
- No event contains free-text PII fields; schema tests enforce it.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 With default settings the game makes zero telemetry network requests (automated e2e).
- EC-2 A playtester can export one bundle file and an analysis script turns N bundles into a death heatmap + spell/puzzle report.
- EC-3 No event contains free-text PII fields; schema tests enforce it.

epics.title: E35 — MVP Fun Validation
epics.description:
## Outcome
External players demonstrate that combat, magic, stealth and exploration are intrinsically enjoyable, measured against fun hypotheses written before testing.
## Scope
- In: Fun hypotheses, playtest protocol, tester recruitment, playtest build channel
- In: Internal greybox and class-fantasy playtests, external rounds, triage, go/no-go decision
- Out: Telemetry tooling (mw-e34)
- Out: Mobile (mw-e36)
## Exit criteria
- Two external rounds with ≥ 8 players each completed and reported.
- Go/no-go decision recorded against the pre-registered hypotheses.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 Two external rounds with ≥ 8 players each completed and reported.
- EC-2 Go/no-go decision recorded against the pre-registered hypotheses.

epics.title: E36 — Mobile Adaptation
epics.description:
## Outcome
Only after MVP validation: touch UX, mobile performance profiles, interface redesign and mobile browser support.
## Scope
- In: Coarse placeholder items to be re-planned after the MVP go decision
- Out: Any mobile work before e35-mvp-go-no-go is decided
## Exit criteria
- A mobile plan is re-scoped into PR-sized beads after the MVP go decision.
epics.acceptance: - EC-1 A mobile plan is re-scoped into PR-sized beads after the MVP go decision.

items.title: Scaffold TypeScript/Vite/pnpm repo with lint, typecheck and Vitest
items.description:
## Why
Every other bead needs a consistent, strict toolchain; rapid iteration (constitution §10) starts with a fast, boring build.
## What
Create the project skeleton: pnpm workspace root, Vite app, TypeScript strict, ESLint (flat config) + Prettier, Vitest with v8 coverage, Playwright installed, and the `src/{sim,content,game,render,audio,ui,tools}` layout from the backlog contract §2 with a placeholder module + test in each. Scripts: `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint`, `format`, `typecheck`, `test`, `test:coverage`, `e2e`.
## Scope
- In: package.json, pnpm-lock, .nvmrc/.node-version, tsconfig (strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes)
- In: ESLint + Prettier config, EditorConfig
- In: vitest.config.ts with v8 coverage (reporters: text, json-summary, lcov)
- In: playwright.config.ts with one placeholder spec
- In: README quickstart section
- Out: CI workflows (e00-ci-pipeline)
- Out: Per-layer thresholds and ratchet (e00-ci-pipeline)
- Out: Determinism lint rules (e00-determinism-lint)
- Out: Renderer dependency (e00-render-bootstrap)
## Notes
- Pin Node LTS via .node-version and `packageManager` field; use corepack.
- Path aliases: `@sim/*`, `@content/*`, `@game/*`… mirrored in Vite and Vitest.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a fresh clone with the pinned Node, when `pnpm install && pnpm build` runs, then it exits 0 and produces `dist/index.html`.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the scaffold, when `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` runs, then all pass with at least one test per `src/*` layer.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a file with an implicit `any` or an unchecked index access, when `pnpm typecheck` runs, then it fails.
- AC-4 [integration] Given `pnpm test:coverage`, when it completes, then `coverage/coverage-summary.json` and `coverage/lcov.info` exist.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given `pnpm e2e`, when the placeholder Playwright spec opens the built app, then the page loads with zero console errors.
- AC-6 [integration] Given a Node version other than the pinned one, when `pnpm install` runs, then it fails with an engine-mismatch message (engine-strict).

items.title: Lint src/sim for nondeterminism and forbidden layer imports
items.description:
## Why
Deterministic sim (constitution §10) is only real if it is mechanically enforced; replays and save stability depend on it.
## What
ESLint overrides scoped to `src/sim/**` banning `Math.random`, `Date.now`, `new Date()`, `performance.now`, `crypto.getRandomValues`, `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`requestAnimationFrame`, `window`/`document`/`navigator` globals, and imports from `src/{game,render,audio,ui,tools}` or renderer/physics-rendering packages. Import-boundary rules for all layers: `render` may not import `ui`, `sim` imports only `sim` + `content` types, etc.
## Scope
- In: eslint no-restricted-globals / no-restricted-properties / no-restricted-syntax rules for src/sim
- In: eslint-plugin-import (or boundaries) layer matrix for all src/* layers
- In: Fixture files under `test/lint-fixtures/` proving each rule fires
- Out: Runtime determinism checks (e00-replay-harness)
## Notes
- Allowed escape: `// eslint-disable-next-line` in src/sim is itself banned via `eslint-comments/no-restricted-disable` for these rules.
- Iteration order: prefer arrays/Maps (insertion ordered); document that `for…in` over numeric-like keys is ordered by spec but discouraged.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a fixture `src/sim` file calling `Math.random()`, `Date.now()` or `performance.now()`, when ESLint runs, then each call is reported as an error naming the injected RNG/clock alternative.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a `src/sim` file importing from `src/render` or referencing `document`, when ESLint runs, then an error is reported.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `src/game` calling `performance.now()`, when ESLint runs, then no error is reported (rule scoped to sim only).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a `src/sim` file with `// eslint-disable-next-line no-restricted-properties` above `Math.random()`, when ESLint runs, then the disable comment itself is reported as an error.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the lint fixture suite, when `pnpm test` runs, then a test programmatically lints every fixture and asserts the expected rule IDs fire.

items.title: Add CI with per-layer coverage gates, ratchet and Playwright smoke
items.description:
## Why
The contract goal is releases trusted without reading the code; that requires CI to enforce the §3 coverage policy mechanically, not by reviewer vigilance.
## What
GitHub Actions workflow `ci.yml` on pull_request and push to main with jobs: `lint` (incl. determinism lint), `typecheck`, `unit` (Vitest + coverage), `coverage-gate`, `coverage-ratchet`, `e2e-smoke` (Playwright, Chromium), `build`. Coverage enforcement:
  1. **100% layer:** `vitest.config.ts` `coverage.thresholds` glob entries for `src/sim/**`, `src/content/**`, `src/game/save/**` (save/load), and runtime dirs registered in `coverage-layers.json` (economy, quest, dialogue runtimes, `scripts/backlog/**`) at 100 lines/branches/functions/statements with `perFile: true`.
  2. **Glue layer:** `src/game/**`, `src/ui/**`, `src/audio/**`, `src/tools/**` at ≥ 90 lines and branches (per directory).
  3. **Excluded layer:** `src/render/**`, shaders, WASM bindings, bootstrap are excluded only if listed in `coverage-exclusions.md` (validated by e00-coverage-exclusions).
  4. **Ratchet:** on push to main CI uploads `coverage-summary.json` as artifact `coverage-baseline`; PR runs download the latest main artifact and `scripts/coverage-ratchet.mjs` fails if any of the four metrics decreases (tolerance 0.01 pp) globally or for any layer in `coverage-layers.json`. If no artifact is available it falls back to committed `coverage-baseline.json` and emits a warning annotation.
## Scope
- In: .github/workflows/ci.yml, pnpm store caching, Playwright browser caching
- In: coverage-layers.json (single source for layer → globs → thresholds) consumed by vitest.config.ts and the ratchet script
- In: scripts/coverage-ratchet.mjs with 100% unit coverage
- In: Job summary table of coverage per layer vs baseline
- Out: Secret scanning and CVE audit jobs (e00-secret-scanning, e00-dependency-audit)
- Out: beads validation job (e00-beads-validate)
- Out: Cross-browser matrix (e32-browser-matrix)
- Out: Required-check configuration (e00-branch-protection)
## Notes
- Stable job names matter: branch protection references them (`lint`, `typecheck`, `unit`, `coverage-gate`, `coverage-ratchet`, `e2e-smoke`, `build`).
- Use `concurrency` to cancel superseded PR runs.
- Adding a new 100%-layer runtime directory = one line in coverage-layers.json.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a PR that adds an uncovered branch in `src/sim`, when CI runs, then `coverage-gate` fails naming the file and metric below 100%.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a PR that drops `src/ui` line coverage to 89%, when CI runs, then `coverage-gate` fails; at 90% it passes.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a baseline summary and a PR summary where global branches fell from 95.20% to 95.10%, when `coverage-ratchet.mjs` runs, then it exits non-zero and prints the metric, layer, old and new values.
- AC-4 [unit] Given no main-branch artifact is available, when the ratchet runs, then it compares against committed `coverage-baseline.json` and emits a GitHub warning annotation instead of silently passing.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a PR summary equal to baseline within 0.01 pp, when the ratchet runs, then it passes (float tolerance).
- AC-6 [integration] Given a PR with a failing Playwright smoke test, when CI runs, then `e2e-smoke` fails and uploads the trace and screenshot as artifacts.
- AC-7 [integration] Given a clean PR, when CI runs with warm caches, then the full pipeline completes in ≤ 10 minutes.

items.title: Enforce coverage-exclusions.md as the only source of exclusions
items.description:
## Why
Exclusions are where coverage policies quietly rot; each one must be visible, justified and owned.
## What
Create `coverage-exclusions.md` with a machine-readable table (path glob | reason | bead | alternative verification). `scripts/check-coverage-exclusions.mjs` parses it and asserts the Vitest `coverage.exclude` list is exactly the set in the file (beyond default test/config ignores), every row has a non-empty reason and a `mw-` bead id, no glob matches `src/sim/**` or `src/content/**`, and glue-layer gaps below 100% are listed with justification. Also bans `/* v8 ignore */` / `istanbul ignore` comments outside excluded paths.
## Scope
- In: coverage-exclusions.md template + initial rows (src/render/**, bootstrap main.ts)
- In: check script + CI step in the coverage-gate job
- In: Docs section in CONTRIBUTING on how to request an exclusion
- Out: Threshold numbers themselves (e00-ci-pipeline)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given vitest excludes `src/render/**` but the markdown table does not list it, when the check runs, then it fails naming the unlisted glob.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a row with an empty reason or without a `mw-` bead id, when the check runs, then it fails naming the row.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a row excluding `src/sim/rng.ts`, when the check runs, then it fails because 100% layers cannot be excluded.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a `/* v8 ignore next */` comment in `src/game/foo.ts` (non-excluded path), when the check runs, then it fails with file and line.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the committed repo state, when CI runs the check, then it passes and the script has 100% coverage.

items.title: Block secrets via gitleaks in CI and an optional pre-commit hook
items.description:
## Why
The repo is public; a leaked token is permanent. Secrets must never reach a commit.
## What
Add a `secrets` CI job running gitleaks over the PR commit range (and full history on push to main), a `.gitleaks.toml` with an allowlist mechanism that requires a comment, enable GitHub secret scanning + push protection in repo settings, and a lefthook/husky pre-commit hook running gitleaks on staged files.
## Scope
- In: .github/workflows/security.yml `secrets` job
- In: .gitleaks.toml
- In: pre-commit hook (opt-in install via `pnpm prepare`)
- In: Enable GitHub secret scanning + push protection (documented; needs-human if API token lacks admin)
- Out: Dependency CVEs (e00-dependency-audit)
## Notes
- Test the job with a fake high-entropy token in a throwaway branch; do not commit real-format tokens into fixtures — use gitleaks test fixtures generated at runtime.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a PR commit containing a string matching the GitHub PAT pattern, when CI runs, then `secrets` fails and reports file and line without echoing the full secret.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a clean PR, when CI runs, then `secrets` passes in ≤ 60 s.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a staged file containing an AWS-key-shaped string, when `git commit` runs with hooks installed, then the commit is rejected.
- AC-4 [manual] Given repository settings, when inspected, then secret scanning and push protection are enabled.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an allowlist entry without an explanatory comment, when the config lint step runs, then it fails.

items.title: Fail CI on CRITICAL dependency CVEs and enable Dependabot
items.description:
## Why
Policy: never ship libraries with known CRITICAL CVEs. A free public game still owes players a safe page.
## What
Add an `audit` CI job (`pnpm audit --audit-level critical --prod` plus dev deps reported) that fails on any CRITICAL advisory, runs on PRs, on push to main and nightly on a schedule. Add Dependabot (npm + github-actions, weekly, grouped minor/patch) and dependency-review-action on PRs to block newly-introduced critical/high-licence problems. Temporary waivers live in `audit-waivers.json` with advisory id, reason, bead and expiry date.
## Scope
- In: security.yml `audit` job + nightly schedule
- In: .github/dependabot.yml
- In: dependency-review-action with licence denylist (GPL-3.0/AGPL for runtime deps, since assets/code must permit free distribution)
- In: audit-waivers.json + validator (expired waiver fails CI)
- Out: Secret scanning (e00-secret-scanning)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a PR adding a dependency version with a known CRITICAL advisory, when CI runs, then `audit` fails listing the advisory id and package path.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a HIGH (not critical) advisory, when CI runs, then `audit` passes but writes a warning to the job summary.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a waiver whose expiry date is in the past, when the waiver validator runs, then it fails naming the advisory.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a waiver missing a bead id or reason, when the validator runs, then it fails.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the nightly schedule, when a new CRITICAL advisory affects main, then the workflow fails and opens/updates a GitHub issue titled with the advisory id.

items.title: Validate .beads/issues.jsonl parses and is well-formed in CI
items.description:
## Why
The backlog is a project artefact that drives backlog.html; a malformed line from a bad merge must be caught before it breaks the page.
## What
Script `scripts/validate-beads.mjs` (100% covered) run in CI job `beads-validate` when `.beads/**` changes (and always on main): every non-empty line parses as JSON; each record has `id`, `title`, `status`; ids match `^mw-`; no duplicate ids (last-wins is reported as an error unless bd format allows it); dependency targets exist; epic children reference an existing epic. Emits GitHub annotations with line numbers.
## Scope
- In: validate script + tests with fixture jsonl files
- In: CI job with path filter plus always-run on main
- Out: Label/AC style linting of bead content (possible follow-up)
## Notes
- Confirm bd issues.jsonl semantics (one line per issue vs append log) when implementing; the duplicate rule must match bd behaviour.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a jsonl with a truncated line 42, when the validator runs, then it exits non-zero with an annotation pointing to line 42.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a record whose dependency references `mw-e99.7` which does not exist, when validated, then it fails naming both ids.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an empty trailing line or CRLF line endings, when validated, then it passes.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the committed `.beads/issues.jsonl`, when CI runs `beads-validate`, then it passes.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the script and fixtures, when coverage runs, then `scripts/validate-beads.mjs` is at 100% on all metrics.

items.title: Add PR template with Closes lines and a PR-body lint check
items.description:
## Why
backlog.html and bead closure rely on explicit `Closes mw-…` lines; they must be present and well-formed on every PR.
## What
Add `.github/pull_request_template.md` (Summary, Closes lines, Test evidence, DoD checklist from contract §3, CHANGELOG note, coverage exclusions touched). Add a `pr-lint` job (pull_request: opened/edited/synchronize) that parses the PR body and fails if there is no `Closes mw-<id>` line (unless label `no-bead` is applied by a maintainer for trivial chores) or if a referenced id does not exist in `.beads/issues.jsonl` on the PR head.
## Scope
- In: PR template
- In: scripts/pr-body-lint.mjs (shared parser with e00-backlog-pr-status, 100% covered)
- In: pr-lint job
- Out: Closing beads after merge (process, CLAUDE.md)
## Notes
- Share the `Closes` regex with the backlog generator: `^\s*Closes\s+(mw-[a-z0-9.]+)\s*$` (case-insensitive, one id per line).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a body with lines `Closes mw-e00.3` and `closes mw-e30.1`, when parsed, then both ids are returned.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a body mentioning `mw-e00.3` only in prose (`fixes part of mw-e00.3`), when parsed, then no ids are returned.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a PR without any Closes line and without the `no-bead` label, when `pr-lint` runs, then it fails with a message showing the expected format.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a PR whose Closes line references an id not in issues.jsonl, when `pr-lint` runs, then it fails naming the id.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the PR body is edited to add a valid Closes line, when the `edited` event fires, then `pr-lint` re-runs and passes.

items.title: Create CHANGELOG.md and a check for user-facing changes
items.description:
## Why
DoD item 8: players and testers need to know what changed between playtest builds.
## What
Add `CHANGELOG.md` (Keep a Changelog format, `Unreleased` section). Add a lightweight CI check: if a PR touches `src/{game,ui,render,audio,sim,content}/**` and has neither a CHANGELOG diff nor the `no-changelog` label, fail with guidance.
## Scope
- In: CHANGELOG.md
- In: changelog check job/script
- Out: Release tagging automation (later, if needed)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a PR modifying `src/sim/foo.ts` without touching CHANGELOG.md or labelling `no-changelog`, when CI runs, then the changelog check fails.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a PR touching only `docs/**` or `.github/**`, when CI runs, then the check passes without a CHANGELOG entry.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a CHANGELOG with no `## [Unreleased]` heading, when the check parses it, then it fails.

items.title: Protect main: squash-only, required checks, auto-delete branches
items.description:
## Why
Contract §1: all work via PR, squash merge only, CI green. Protection makes that a rule rather than a habit.
## What
Configure (and codify in `scripts/configure-repo.sh` using `gh api`) main branch protection: require PR, require status checks `lint`, `typecheck`, `unit`, `coverage-gate`, `coverage-ratchet`, `e2e-smoke`, `build`, `secrets`, `audit`, `beads-validate`, `pr-lint`; require branches up to date; disallow force-push and deletion; squash merge only (merge commits and rebase disabled); auto-delete head branches; linear history. Document the settings in `docs/repo-settings.md`.
## Scope
- In: configure-repo.sh (idempotent) + docs
- In: Verification script that reads settings via API and diffs against expected
- Out: Adding new checks later (each check bead updates the script)
## Notes
- Solo-maintainer project: do not require approving reviews (would block the only maintainer); rely on required checks. Revisit if contributors join.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given repository settings, when a direct push to main is attempted, then it is rejected.
- AC-2 [manual] Given a PR with a failing required check, when merge is attempted, then GitHub blocks it.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the verify script, when run against the repo, then it reports zero drift from expected settings (squash-only, required checks list, auto-delete on).
- AC-4 [manual] Given a PR merged via the UI, when it completes, then only "Squash and merge" was offered and the head branch was deleted.
- AC-5 [integration] Given configure-repo.sh run twice, when the second run completes, then it makes no changes (idempotent).

items.title: Generate backlog.html from issues.jsonl and deploy to GitHub Pages
items.description:
## Why
A human-friendly public view of what is done and what is next keeps the project honest and lets playtesters and collaborators follow progress without installing bd.
## What
As a developer or follower, I want a single-file backlog.html with Completed and Upcoming / In progress tabs so that I can see progress per epic and milestone at a glance.
`scripts/backlog/generate.mjs` reads `.beads/issues.jsonl` and writes `site/backlog.html` (also served as `index.html`): one self-contained file (inline CSS/JS, no external requests), two tabs "Completed" and "Upcoming / In progress", grouped by epic then milestone, each bead showing ID, title, priority, status, labels, expandable ACs and description (`<details>`), and dependencies (linked in-page, with blocker status). Per-epic progress bar (closed/total). Generated-at timestamp and source commit SHA. Workflow `.github/workflows/backlog-pages.yml` builds and deploys to GitHub Pages on push to main and `workflow_dispatch`.
## Scope
- In: Generator (pure functions: parse → model → render) with 100% coverage (listed in coverage-layers.json)
- In: HTML escaping of all bead text; a safe minimal markdown subset (headings, lists, code, bold) rendered without raw HTML passthrough
- In: Pages workflow using actions/upload-pages-artifact + actions/deploy-pages with `concurrency: pages`
- In: Light/dark theme via prefers-color-scheme; readable at 375 px width
- Out: GitHub PR overlay (merged/open PR status) and pull_request_target trigger — see e00-backlog-pr-status
- Out: Issue-editing UI (read-only page)
## Notes
- Status mapping: closed → Completed; open/in_progress/blocked/deferred → Upcoming tab with status pill; epics sorted by id, milestones m0→post-mvp, then priority, then id.
- Keep render pure and deterministic given (issues, prStatus, now, sha) so snapshot tests are stable.
- Workflow permissions: `contents: read`, `pages: write`, `id-token: write`.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a jsonl with one closed and two open beads under `mw-e09`, when generated, then the Completed tab lists 1 and the Upcoming tab lists 2 under the E09 heading with a 1/3 progress bar.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a bead title containing `<script>alert(1)</script>`, when rendered, then the output contains the escaped text and no executable script element from bead content.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a bead with acceptance criteria, when rendered, then the ACs appear inside a collapsed `<details>` element and the bead row shows ID, priority, status, labels and dependency links.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a bead depending on an id not present in the file, when rendered, then the dependency shows as "unknown" rather than throwing.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an empty issues.jsonl, when generated, then both tabs render an empty-state message and the script exits 0.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the generated file, when opened in Playwright with network disabled, then it renders fully, tab switching works by click and keyboard, and there are zero console errors.
- AC-7 [integration] Given a push to main, when backlog-pages.yml runs, then the Pages URL serves the new file within that run; `workflow_dispatch` produces the same result.
- AC-8 [integration] Given coverage runs, when complete, then `scripts/backlog/**` is at 100% lines/branches/functions/statements.

items.title: Reflect merged/open PR Closes lines in backlog.html immediately
items.description:
## Why
Beads are closed locally after merge, so issues.jsonl lags reality; the public page must be accurate the moment a PR merges.
## What
As a follower, I want beads referenced by merged PRs to appear as Completed (with a PR link) and beads in open PRs to appear In progress so that the page is correct even before local bead closure is pushed.
The generator gains a GitHub overlay: using `GITHUB_TOKEN`, list PRs (paginated, REST or GraphQL), parse `Closes mw-…` lines with the shared parser from e00-pr-template, and compute: merged PR → bead Completed with link "PR #N" and merge date; open PR → bead In progress with link; closed-unmerged PR → ignored. Bead closed in jsonl wins over open-PR status. The Pages workflow adds `pull_request_target` (types: opened, reopened, edited, closed) so the page updates on PR open/close; under pull_request_target it checks out the default branch only and never checks out or executes PR code.
## Scope
- In: scripts/backlog/github.mjs with injectable fetch, pagination and rate-limit handling (100% covered, fixture-based tests)
- In: Overlay merge rules + "source" badges (jsonl vs PR)
- In: Workflow trigger changes with `permissions: pull-requests: read` and explicit `ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}`
- In: Offline flag `--no-github` for local runs
- Out: Automatically closing beads in jsonl from CI (process stays local per CLAUDE.md)
## Notes
- Security: pull_request_target runs with a write-capable token in base context — never `actions/checkout` with `ref: github.event.pull_request.head.sha`, never run scripts from the PR; the PR body is treated as untrusted data (only regex-extracted ids are used).
- Cache API responses per run; cap to last 500 PRs by default.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given jsonl bead `mw-e09.3` open and a merged PR #57 whose body has `Closes mw-e09.3`, when generated, then `mw-e09.3` is in the Completed tab with a link to PR #57.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an open PR #60 with `Closes mw-e09.4`, when generated, then `mw-e09.4` shows status "in progress (PR #60)" in the Upcoming tab.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a closed-unmerged PR referencing `mw-e09.5`, when generated, then `mw-e09.5` keeps its jsonl status.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the GitHub API returns 403 rate-limited or a network error, when generated, then the page is still produced from jsonl alone with a visible "GitHub status unavailable" banner and exit code 0.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a PR body referencing an id not present in jsonl, when generated, then it is listed in an "Unknown references" footer instead of crashing.
- AC-6 [unit] Given 3 pages of PR results, when fetched, then all pages are consumed via the Link header and results merged.
- AC-7 [integration] Given the workflow file, when statically checked by a test, then no step under pull_request_target checks out a PR head ref or runs `pnpm install` from PR contents.
- AC-8 [integration] Given a PR is merged on GitHub, when the resulting workflow run completes, then the Pages site shows its beads as Completed without any local bd action.

items.title: Spike: choose Three.js vs Babylon.js and physics engine (ADR-0001)
items.description:
## Why
The renderer and physics choice shapes every render, animation and physics story; making it on evidence against our hardware baseline avoids a costly mid-project switch.
## What
Time-box: 3 days. Question: which of Three.js + Rapier or Babylon.js + (Rapier | Havok) best serves a stylized third-person action RPG in the browser given our baseline? Build the same benchmark scene in `spikes/engine-three/` and `spikes/engine-babylon/`: greybox dungeon room, 1 skinned glTF character with 3 blended animations + 30 skinned NPCs, 200 dynamic rigid bodies (boxes/barrels) with collisions, 8 dynamic point lights + 1 shadowed directional light, 1 particle emitter, post-processing bloom. Measure on the reference machine (High, 1440p-equivalent) and a low-tier machine if available: p50/p95 frame time, gzip bundle size, time-to-first-frame, JS heap. Evaluate physics determinism: Rapier deterministic build (`@dimforge/rapier3d-deterministic`) snapshot/restore and cross-browser state-hash equality, and whether gameplay physics can live behind the `src/sim` boundary. Also score TS ergonomics, glTF/animation retargeting, inspector/debug tooling, WebGPU path, docs/community, licence.
## Scope
- In: Two spike prototypes (not production code), scripted benchmark harness, results table
- In: docs/adr/0001-engine-and-physics.md with weighted scorecard, decision, consequences, rejected option and revisit triggers
- In: docs/adr/README.md + ADR template (first ADR)
- Out: Production renderer bootstrap (e00-render-bootstrap)
- Out: 3D asset sourcing pipeline (e37-3d-pipeline-decision)
## Notes
- Keep spike code out of src/ and out of coverage; delete or archive after the ADR merges.
- Related: e37-3d-pipeline-decision should consume the glTF/animation findings.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given both prototypes, when run on the reference machine with the scripted harness, then a results table (p50/p95 frame time, bundle gz KB, TTFF, heap) for each is recorded in the ADR with browser/OS versions.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the Rapier deterministic build, when the same 600-step input script runs twice in Chrome and once in Firefox, then the ADR records whether final state hashes match, with the script committed in `spikes/`.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the evaluation, when ADR-0001 is written, then it contains a weighted scorecard, the chosen renderer and physics engine, rejected options with reasons, and explicit revisit triggers.
- AC-4 [manual] Given neither option reaches p95 ≤ 16.7 ms in the benchmark on High, when the ADR is written, then it records the gap, the mitigations assumed (e.g. LOD, instancing, fewer shadow casters) and proposes budget changes rather than silently accepting.
- AC-5 [manual] Given the ADR, when merged, then the ADR states whether gameplay physics runs inside `src/sim` (deterministic) or in `src/game` with sim-owned outcomes, and the contract's "the renderer" wording remains valid.

items.title: Implement seeded RNG streams and injected clock for the sim
items.description:
## Why
Determinism starts with randomness and time being inputs, not ambient globals — required for replays, saves and reproducible bugs.
## What
Add `src/sim/rng`: a fast, serializable PRNG (e.g. PCG32 or xoshiro128**) with named sub-streams (`rng.stream("loot")`) so adding a consumer in one system does not perturb others; helpers (int range, float, chance, pick, shuffle, weighted). Add `src/sim/clock`: a sim clock advanced only by the fixed-step loop (tick count, sim time in ms as integer ticks × step).
## Scope
- In: PRNG with serialize/restore state
- In: Named stream derivation from a root seed (hash of seed + name)
- In: Sim clock type used by all systems
- Out: The loop itself (e00-sim-core)
## Notes
- Avoid Math.* transcendental functions in RNG; use 32-bit integer ops (`Math.imul`, `>>> 0`) which are specified exactly.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given seed 12345, when 1,000 values are drawn from stream "loot", then they equal a committed golden sequence.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a stream whose state is serialized after 500 draws and restored into a new instance, when 500 more draws are made, then they equal the original instance's next 500.
- AC-3 [unit] Given streams "loot" and "ai", when extra draws are added to "ai", then the "loot" sequence is unchanged.
- AC-4 [unit] Given `int(5, 5)` or `pick([])`, when called, then it returns 5 and throws a typed `EmptyChoiceError` respectively.
- AC-5 [unit] Given 1,000,000 `float()` draws, when bucketed into 10 bins, then each bin holds 10% ± 0.5%.

items.title: Build deterministic fixed-step sim loop, entity store and event bus
items.description:
## Why
Every rule of the game (constitution: systemic world, "Wait… I can do that?") lives in one deterministic, testable simulation core.
## What
Add `src/sim/core`: `World` with fixed timestep (default 60 Hz, configurable), ordered system scheduler, entity/component store (typed component definitions, stable integer entity ids, dense storage, queries with deterministic iteration order), deferred entity creation/destruction applied at end of tick, and a typed event bus (events emitted during tick N are delivered in emission order at defined phase boundaries). `step(inputs)` is the only way time advances; inputs are a per-tick command list.
## Scope
- In: World, scheduler, component registry, queries, event bus, command/input queue
- In: Snapshot/restore API hook for components (consumed by state hash and saves)
- In: Micro-benchmarks via `vitest bench`
- Out: Canonical state hashing (e00-sim-state-hash)
- Out: Render interpolation and rAF binding (e00-game-loop-bridge)
- Out: Physics integration (per ADR-0001)
## Notes
- Entity ids are never reused within a session (generation counter) to avoid stale-reference bugs.
- Cross-browser float determinism is not guaranteed for Math.sin/cos/exp; document the policy: determinism target is same build + same engine; gameplay-critical trig goes through `src/sim/math` wrappers so a deterministic implementation can be swapped in.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given systems A, B, C registered in that order, when `step()` runs, then they execute in order A→B→C every tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an entity destroyed by system A during tick N, when system B queries in the same tick, then the entity is still visible, and from tick N+1 it is gone.
- AC-3 [unit] Given two worlds with the same seed and identical input lists for 1,000 ticks, when compared, then their component snapshots are deep-equal.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an event emitted by a handler of another event, when the bus flushes, then the nested event is delivered after the current event in FIFO order and a cycle guard throws after 10,000 events in one flush.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a query for components [Position, Flammable], when entities are added in random order, then iteration order is ascending entity id.
- AC-6 [perf] Given 5,000 entities with 3 components and 10 trivial systems, when `vitest bench` runs in Node on CI, then mean `step()` time is ≤ 1 ms.

items.title: Add canonical sim state serialization and hashing
items.description:
## Why
Replays, save verification and desync debugging all need one canonical, order-independent fingerprint of sim state.
## What
Add `src/sim/snapshot`: canonical serialization of world state (sorted entity ids, component fields in declared order, floats encoded via their IEEE-754 bits, RNG states, clock) and a fast non-cryptographic hash (e.g. xxHash32/FNV-1a 64) over it. Provide `diffSnapshots(a, b)` returning the first differing entity/component/field for debugging.
## Scope
- In: Canonical encoder, hash, diff utility
- Out: Save file format (e30-save-serialization reuses the encoder)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given two worlds with identical state built via different entity insertion orders but the same ids, when hashed, then the hashes are equal.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a single component float differing by 1 ULP, when hashed, then the hashes differ and `diffSnapshots` names the entity, component and field.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `-0` vs `+0` and two different NaN payloads, when encoded, then the documented canonicalisation rule is applied consistently (NaN canonicalised; ±0 distinct) and tested.
- AC-4 [perf] Given 5,000 entities × 3 components, when hashed in Node, then it completes in ≤ 5 ms.

items.title: Record inputs and replay them to identical state hashes in tests
items.description:
## Why
Contract §3 determinism policy: recorded input logs must replay to identical sim state hashes — our strongest regression net for emergent systems.
## What
Add `src/sim/replay`: a replay file format (`{formatVersion, buildSha, contentHash, seed, stepHz, inputs: per-tick command lists (run-length encoded), checkpoints: [{tick, hash}]}`), a recorder that captures commands fed to `World.step`, and a player that re-runs them asserting checkpoint hashes. Vitest helper `expectReplay("replays/foo.json")` and a `pnpm replay:record` dev hook in the game layer. Golden replays live in `test/replays/` and run in CI.
## Scope
- In: Format (zod schema), recorder, player, checkpoint every N ticks (default 60)
- In: Vitest helper + one golden replay against the core sim
- In: Clear failure output using `diffSnapshots` at the first mismatching checkpoint
- Out: Bug-report capture UX (e33-replay-bug-capture)
- Out: Game-layer keyboard/mouse capture (lives with e02-input-actions integration)
## Notes
- Replays record *sim commands* (post input mapping), not raw DOM events, so they survive key remapping.
- When content or sim changes intentionally alter outcomes, `pnpm replay:rebless` regenerates hashes and the diff must be reviewed in the PR.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a recorded 3,600-tick session, when replayed, then every checkpoint hash matches and the final hash equals the recorded final hash.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a sim change that alters one component at tick 1,234, when the golden replay runs, then it fails reporting checkpoint tick 1,260 (first after divergence) and the differing entity/field.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a replay whose `formatVersion` is newer than supported, when loaded, then it fails with a typed `UnsupportedReplayVersion` error.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a replay whose `contentHash` differs from current content, when run, then the harness reports "content changed" distinctly from a determinism failure.
- AC-5 [integration] Given `test/replays/*.json`, when CI runs unit tests, then all golden replays execute and pass.

items.title: Load schema-validated content with a per-entry test harness
items.description:
## Why
Spells, items, creatures and puzzles are data, not code (constitution §10); designers need fast, safe iteration with errors caught before runtime.
## What
Add `src/content`: a registry of content types, each with a zod schema and a folder under `content/<type>/*.json`; a loader (Vite `import.meta.glob` in the app, fs in Node tests) that validates, reports all errors with file path + JSON path, and freezes results into a typed, id-indexed catalogue. Cross-reference helper (`ref("creature", id)`) validated after load. Content hash over canonical content for replay/save compatibility. Test harness: `describeContent("spell", (entry) => …)` generates one test per entry, and a coverage check fails if any content entry has no exercising test.
## Scope
- In: Registry, loader, error formatting, cross-ref validation, content hash
- In: Example content type `testprop` with 2 entries
- In: Per-entry test generator + "every entry exercised" check
- In: JSON Schema export from zod for editor autocompletion (`content/*.schema.json`)
- Out: Specific schemas (spells e06, creatures e12, items e17, …)
- Out: CLI validator/scaffolder and hot reload (e33-content-validator-cli, e33-content-scaffolder, e33-content-hot-reload)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a content file with a missing required field and a wrong type in two places, when loaded, then all three errors are reported with file path and JSON pointer in one run.
- AC-2 [unit] Given two entries with the same id in different files, when loaded, then loading fails naming both files.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an entry referencing `creature:goblin-archer` that does not exist, when cross-refs validate, then it fails naming source entry and missing target.
- AC-4 [unit] Given unchanged content in a different file order, when the content hash is computed, then it is identical.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a content entry with no test that exercises it, when the content-coverage check runs in CI, then it fails listing the entry id.
- AC-6 [content] Given the example `testprop` entries, when validated, then they pass and the loaded catalogue is deeply frozen.

items.title: Bootstrap the chosen renderer and physics with a boot smoke test
items.description:
## Why
The ADR decision must become a running, measurable baseline before any visual gameplay work begins.
## What
Install the renderer and physics chosen in ADR-0001; add `src/render/bootstrap` creating canvas, renderer, scene, camera, resize/DPR handling (render scale setting hook) and a clear teardown; lazy-load the physics WASM with a loading state. Playwright smoke: app boots, first frame renders, no console errors, canvas non-blank (pixel sample check), resize works.
## Scope
- In: Renderer + physics bootstrap, dispose(), DPR cap
- In: Unsupported-browser fallback screen (WebGL2/WASM missing) — minimal version
- In: Playwright boot smoke spec with screenshot artifact
- In: coverage-exclusions.md row for render bootstrap
- Out: Full capability detection matrix (e32-capability-detection)
- Out: Greybox content (e00-greybox-testbed)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the built app, when loaded in Chromium, then the first frame renders within 3 s locally, the canvas has non-uniform pixels, and there are zero console errors or warnings from our code.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the viewport resizes from 1280×720 to 1920×1080, when the next frame renders, then canvas drawing-buffer size matches viewport × min(devicePixelRatio, cap).
- AC-3 [e2e] Given WebAssembly is disabled via init script, when the app loads, then a readable "unsupported browser" screen appears instead of a blank page or uncaught error.
- AC-4 [integration] Given `dispose()` is called, when the renderer is recreated 5 times, then WebGL context count does not grow and no errors are logged.

items.title: Bind fixed-step sim to rAF rendering with interpolation
items.description:
## Why
Smooth visuals at any refresh rate with a deterministic sim underneath is the backbone of "responsive controls feel excellent" (E02).
## What
Add `src/game/loop`: an accumulator-based loop on requestAnimationFrame that advances `World.step` at the fixed rate, caps catch-up steps (spiral-of-death guard), exposes interpolation alpha to render sync, and pauses the sim when the tab is hidden. Render sync reads sim snapshots (read-only view) and updates scene objects. Input sampling produces per-tick command lists (hook for e02-input-actions).
## Scope
- In: Loop, accumulator, max-steps-per-frame cap, pause/resume on visibilitychange
- In: Sim→render sync interface (entity ↔ scene object binding registry)
- In: Injected time source for tests
- Out: Action mapping (e02-input-actions)
- Out: Frame pacing analytics (e32-frame-pacing)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a fake clock advancing 33.3 ms per frame at 60 Hz sim, when 60 frames run, then exactly 120 sim steps occur and alpha stays in [0,1).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a single frame delta of 2,000 ms (debugger pause), when the loop processes it, then at most 5 steps run and the excess time is dropped with a logged warning.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `visibilitychange` to hidden, when 10 s pass and the tab becomes visible, then 0 sim steps ran while hidden and no catch-up burst occurs.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a 144 Hz and a 60 Hz simulated display, when the same inputs run for 600 sim ticks, then final sim state hashes are identical.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an entity destroyed in the sim, when render sync runs, then its bound scene object is disposed within the same frame.

items.title: Create greybox testbed scene, level kit, scene loader and debug camera
items.description:
## Why
Gameplay is never blocked by art; every system needs a fast place to be tried in-engine from day one.
## What
As a developer, I want a greybox testbed and modular level kit so that I can prototype rooms, corridors and encounters in minutes.
Greybox kit primitives (floor, wall, ramp, stairs, pillar, doorway, platform, crate) with grid snapping and colour-coded materials by purpose (walkable, climbable, interactive, hazard). Scenes are data (`content/scenes/*.json`: placements + entity spawns) loaded by a scene loader into both sim and renderer. Free-fly debug camera (toggle), scene picker via `?scene=` URL param, and a default `testbed` scene (room → corridor → arena).
## Scope
- In: Level kit + scene schema (via e00-content-pipeline)
- In: Scene loader/unloader (sim entities + render objects + physics colliders)
- In: Debug fly camera, `?scene=` param, on-screen scene name + build SHA
- In: Playwright smoke loading each scene in `content/scenes`
- Out: Player controller and gameplay camera (e02-player-controller, e02-camera)
- Out: Debug console (e33-debug-console)
## Notes
- Scenes may be authored by hand in JSON or exported from Blender via glTF extras later; keep the schema simple.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given `?scene=testbed`, when the app loads, then the room→corridor→arena scene renders with zero console errors within 5 s locally.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a scene file, when loaded then unloaded, then the sim world has zero remaining scene entities and the physics world zero colliders.
- AC-3 [content] Given every file in `content/scenes`, when validated, then it passes the scene schema and all referenced kit pieces exist.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given `?scene=does-not-exist`, when loaded, then a visible error lists available scenes and the app does not crash.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the debug camera toggled on, when WASD/mouse input is sent, then the camera moves and toggling off restores the prior camera.
- AC-6 [perf] Given the testbed scene, when measured on the reference machine (High), then p95 frame time ≤ 8 ms (half budget, leaving headroom for gameplay).

items.title: Write CONTRIBUTING.md covering worktrees, beads, DoD and ADRs
items.description:
## Why
Humans and agents both contribute; one short guide prevents process drift (wrong branch, missing Closes lines, unsigned commits).
## What
Document: worktree-per-branch flow, bead lifecycle (claim → PR with Closes lines → close after merge), commit sign-off (DCO), squash-merge, DoD, coverage layers and how to request an exclusion, determinism rules for src/sim, ADR process (docs/adr), CHANGELOG convention, how to regenerate backlog.html locally. Add a DCO check job if sign-off is required.
## Scope
- In: CONTRIBUTING.md, link from README and AGENTS.md
- In: DCO check (GitHub DCO app or action) as a required check
- Out: Code of conduct / licence choice (separate decision if needed)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given a new contributor following only CONTRIBUTING.md, when they make a trivial change, then they produce a PR with a Closes line, signed-off commit and green CI without further guidance.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a PR with an unsigned commit, when CI runs, then the DCO check fails.
- AC-3 [integration] Given markdown link checking, when CI runs on docs changes, then CONTRIBUTING.md has no broken relative links.

items.title: Define versioned save format with section registry and migrations
items.description:
## Why
Save-game stability is a constitution technical priority; one versioned format with a migration chain prevents "your save is incompatible" after every update.
## What
Add `src/game/save/format` (100% coverage layer): save envelope `{formatVersion, saveSchemaVersion, gameVersion, buildSha, contentHash, createdAtTick, wallClockSavedAt (injected), metadata, sections: Record<sectionId, {version, data}>, checksum}`. Systems register a section (`registerSaveSection({id, version, schema, serialize(world), deserialize(world, data), migrations})`). Serialization reuses the canonical encoder from e00-sim-state-hash; checksum over sections. Migration runner applies per-section migrations in order (vN→vN+1) before zod validation.
## Scope
- In: Envelope schema (zod), section registry, serialize/deserialize whole world
- In: Per-section migration chain + runner
- In: Checksum verification
- In: Round-trip property test: random world → save → load → identical state hash
- Out: Persistence to IndexedDB (e30-indexeddb-storage)
- Out: Fixture-based migration CI harness (e30-migration-fixtures)
- Out: World facts content (e27-world-state-store registers its own section)
## Notes
- Sections allow e17 inventory, e27 world state, e19 progression, e23 quests to own their data without a central god-schema.
- Unknown sections from a newer build are preserved verbatim on re-save (forward-compat) but flagged.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a world with 3 registered sections, when saved and loaded into a fresh world, then the sim state hash equals the original.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a section at data version 1 and code at version 3, when loaded, then migrations 1→2 and 2→3 run in order and the result validates against the v3 schema.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a save whose checksum does not match its sections, when loaded, then a typed `SaveCorruptError` is returned and the world is untouched.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a save containing a section id not registered in this build, when loaded, then load succeeds, a warning lists the unknown section, and re-saving preserves it verbatim.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a missing migration step (v1 data, only 2→3 registered), when loaded, then a typed `MissingMigrationError` names section and versions.
- AC-6 [unit] Given `saveSchemaVersion` newer than the running build supports, when loaded, then it refuses with `SaveFromNewerBuildError` rather than attempting to parse.

items.title: Persist saves to IndexedDB with atomic writes and fallbacks
items.description:
## Why
Browser storage is fragile (quota, private mode, eviction); saves must survive or fail loudly, never silently.
## What
Add `src/game/save/storage`: a `SaveStore` interface with an IndexedDB implementation (db `mw-saves`, stores `slots`, `blobs`) using single-transaction atomic writes (write new blob + update slot pointer in one transaction, keep previous blob as backup), `navigator.storage.persist()` request on first save, quota estimate, and an in-memory fallback when IndexedDB is unavailable with a visible "saves will not persist" warning.
## Scope
- In: IndexedDB store (idb wrapper or hand-rolled), in-memory store, shared contract tests run against both (fake-indexeddb in Node)
- In: Quota and persist-permission handling
- Out: Slot UX (e30-save-slots)
- Out: Cross-tab locking (e30-multi-tab-guard)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the IndexedDB store, when a save is written then read back, then bytes are identical (contract test runs against both implementations).
- AC-2 [integration] Given a transaction aborted mid-write (simulated), when the slot is read, then the previous save is returned intact.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a QuotaExceededError on write, when saving, then the error surfaces as a typed `SaveQuotaError`, the previous save remains, and the UI can show "free up space".
- AC-4 [e2e] Given IndexedDB throws on open (private-mode simulation), when the game starts, then the in-memory store is used and a persistent warning banner is shown.
- AC-5 [integration] Given `navigator.storage.persist` is unavailable, when first save occurs, then saving proceeds without error.

items.title: Gate save-schema changes on committed migration fixtures in CI
items.description:
## Why
Contract §3: versioned migration tests for every save-schema change; forgetting a migration must be impossible, not merely discouraged.
## What
Commit `test/save-fixtures/<saveSchemaVersion>/*.json` generated from representative worlds. A CI test loads every fixture through the current migration chain and asserts it validates and loads. A schema fingerprint (hash of each section's JSON Schema export) is committed in `save-schema.lock.json`; if a section schema changes without bumping its version and adding a migration + fixture, CI fails with instructions. `pnpm save:fixture` generates a fixture for the current version.
## Scope
- In: Fixture loader test, schema fingerprint lock + check, fixture generator script
- Out: Runtime migration logic (e30-save-serialization)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given fixtures for versions 1..N, when CI runs, then each loads under the current build and yields a world passing invariant checks.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a section schema field added without bumping the section version, when the lock check runs, then it fails naming the section and telling the developer to bump + add migration + fixture.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a version bump without a new fixture directory, when the check runs, then it fails.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a fixture that fails to load, when CI runs, then the failure names fixture path and the migration step that threw.

items.title: Support manual save slots with metadata and thumbnails
items.description:
## Why
Players experiment ("what if I anger the minotaur?"); multiple slots make experimentation safe.
## What
As a player, I want several named save slots showing class, location, playtime and a thumbnail so that I can keep parallel playthroughs.
Slot model: 10 manual slots + autosave ring + quicksave; metadata (character name, class, area name, playtime ticks, saved-at, game version, 256×144 WebP thumbnail captured from the canvas). Operations: save, load, overwrite (confirm), delete (confirm), rename.
## Scope
- In: Slot manager in game layer
- In: Thumbnail capture (render-side, excluded-coverage helper)
- Out: Menu UI screens (e30-save-load-ui)
## Notes
- None.

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — required by the E01 grey-box vertical slice.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 10 filled manual slots, when the player attempts an 11th new save, then the slot manager requires choosing an overwrite target.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a slot saved with class knight in area "testbed-arena" after 3,600 ticks, when metadata is read, then it reports those values and playtime 60 s.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a thumbnail capture fails (canvas tainted or context lost), when saving, then the save still succeeds with a placeholder thumbnail.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a slot deletion, when confirmed, then the slot and its backup blob are both removed.

items.title: Autosave on area transitions and checkpoints into a rotating ring
items.description:
## Why
Failure should create stories, not lost hours; autosaves keep risk fun rather than punishing.
## What
As a player, I want the game to autosave at safe moments so that a crash or death never costs much progress.
Autosave triggers: area transition, checkpoint trigger volumes, after quest state changes, and every 5 minutes of playtime when safe. Never while in combat/alerted state, mid-air, or during dialogue — deferred until safe. Ring of 3 autosave slots, oldest overwritten. Unobtrusive HUD indicator.
## Scope
- In: Autosave scheduler with "safe to save" predicate supplied by systems
- In: Ring buffer slots
- In: HUD indicator hook
- Out: Trigger volume implementation (e03-triggers)
- Out: Alert/combat state source (e11-alert-states)
## Notes
- Safe predicate is a registry so combat/stealth/dialogue can veto without save code knowing them.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 3 autosaves exist, when a 4th autosave occurs, then the oldest is replaced and the other two remain.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an autosave trigger fires while a registered veto (combat) is active, when the veto clears 20 s later, then exactly one autosave occurs at that point.
- AC-3 [unit] Given playtime passes 5 minutes with no other autosave, when safe, then a timed autosave occurs; given another autosave happened 1 minute ago, then the timer resets.
- AC-4 [integration] Given an autosave write fails, when the next safe moment arrives, then it retries once and surfaces a non-blocking HUD warning on second failure.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the testbed with a checkpoint volume, when the player enters it, then an autosave appears in the slot list with the area name.

items.title: Add quicksave and quickload actions
items.description:
## Why
Experimentation-heavy play (constitution: "too useful" spells) benefits from instant save-scumming for players who want it.
## What
As a player, I want quicksave/quickload keys so that I can try risky ideas instantly.
Quicksave writes the single quicksave slot (subject to the same safety vetoes as autosave, except combat is allowed); quickload asks for confirmation if unsaved progress > 60 s.
## Scope
- In: Quicksave/quickload actions registered in the action map
- In: Confirmation prompt
- Out: Default key bindings list (e02-input-actions)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given quicksave during combat, when triggered, then the save succeeds (combat not vetoed for quicksave) but mid-air/dialogue still vetoes with a HUD message.
- AC-2 [integration] Given no quicksave exists, when quickload is pressed, then a "no quicksave" toast appears and nothing else changes.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given progress of 90 s since the last save, when quickload is pressed, then a confirmation dialog appears before loading.

items.title: On death, offer reload of latest save or checkpoint
items.description:
## Why
The m1 loop requires die → reload; it must be fast so failure invites another try.
## What
As a player, I want a death screen offering "Load last save" (most recent of any slot type) and "Load…" so that I return to play within seconds.
Death screen appears after the death sequence; reload completes to playable in ≤ 3 s warm.
## Scope
- In: Death screen flow, most-recent-save resolution, full world teardown/rebuild on load
- Out: Death conditions and animation (e04-damage-model and E02)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an autosave at t=100 and a manual save at t=120, when resolving "last save", then the manual save is chosen.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the player dies in the testbed, when "Load last save" is chosen, then the game is playable in ≤ 3 s and the sim state hash equals the save's state hash.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given no saves exist at death, when the death screen shows, then it offers "Restart area" instead and does not error.
- AC-4 [integration] Given load of a corrupt latest save, when chosen from death screen, then the recovery flow (e30-corruption-recovery) offers the backup.

items.title: Recover from corrupt saves using backups and clear messaging
items.description:
## Why
Nothing kills goodwill faster than a lost 10-hour save; recovery must be automatic and honest.
## What
As a player, I want the game to fall back to a backup when a save is damaged so that I never lose everything.
On `SaveCorruptError`/migration failure: try the slot's backup blob, then the next most recent save; show what was restored and its age; offer to export the corrupt file for a bug report.
## Scope
- In: Recovery chain, messaging, corrupt-file export
- Out: General export/import (e30-export-import)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a slot whose primary blob fails checksum and whose backup is valid, when loaded, then the backup loads and the UI states "restored backup from <time>".
- AC-2 [integration] Given primary and backup both corrupt, when loaded, then the next most recent valid save across slots is offered.
- AC-3 [integration] Given all saves corrupt, when loading, then the player can start a new game and export the corrupt files; the game does not crash.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a migration that throws, when loading, then it is treated like corruption (recovery chain) and the error is logged to local telemetry.

items.title: Prevent two open tabs from clobbering each other's saves
items.description:
## Why
Browser games are easily opened twice; concurrent writers silently overwrite progress.
## What
Use the Web Locks API (fallback: BroadcastChannel heartbeat) to elect a single "active" tab. A second tab shows "Game already open in another tab" with a "Play here instead" option that asks the first tab to release (it autosaves and pauses).
## Scope
- In: Lock acquisition, takeover protocol, fallback
- Out: Cross-device sync (not planned)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the game open in tab A, when opened in tab B, then B shows the already-open message and makes no writes.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given B chooses "Play here instead", when A receives the request, then A autosaves, pauses with a notice, and B loads that autosave.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given tab A crashes (closed abruptly), when tab B retries, then it acquires the lock within 5 s.

items.title: Export and import save files
items.description:
## Why
Browser storage can be cleared; players and playtesters need a way to back up and share saves.
## What
As a player, I want to export a save to a file and import it later so that clearing browser data does not erase my adventure.
Export produces `merlins-wrath-<slot>-<date>.mwsave` (JSON envelope, gzip). Import validates envelope, checksum and version, then runs migrations and places it into a chosen slot.
## Scope
- In: Export/import in settings/load menu
- In: Validation errors shown in plain language
- Out: Cloud sync
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given an exported save, when imported into a fresh profile, then loading it yields the same sim state hash.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a file that is not a save (random JSON or PNG), when imported, then a clear "not a Merlin's Wrath save" error is shown and no slot changes.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a save from an older schema version, when imported, then migrations run and it loads.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a save file larger than 20 MB, when imported, then it is rejected before parsing.

items.title: Build Continue / Load / Save menu screens
items.description:
## Why
The m1 loop needs saves reachable from the title screen and pause menu.
## What
As a player, I want Continue, Load and Save screens so that I can resume and manage my saves.
Title: Continue (most recent), New Game, Load. Pause: Save, Load. Slot list shows thumbnail + metadata; confirmation dialogs for overwrite/delete; keyboard and gamepad navigable.
## Scope
- In: Title and pause menu save screens
- In: Empty/error states
- Out: Settings screens (e31-settings-framework)
## Notes
- None.

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — required by the E01 grey-box vertical slice.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given one or more saves, when the title screen shows, then Continue is focused by default and loads the most recent save.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given no saves, when the title screen shows, then Continue is hidden and New Game is focused.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the slot list, when navigated by keyboard only (arrows/Enter/Esc), then every action (load, save, overwrite confirm, delete confirm) is reachable.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the storage in in-memory fallback mode, when the save screen opens, then the non-persistence warning is visible.

items.title: Create typed settings store and options menu skeleton
items.description:
## Why
Every accessibility and comfort feature needs one place to live, persist and notify systems of change.
## What
Add `src/game/settings`: a zod-typed settings schema with defaults and categories (controls, camera, display, audio, accessibility, gameplay/difficulty), versioned persistence in localStorage (small, sync) with migration, change subscriptions (`settings.on("camera.invertY", cb)`), and "apply immediately" semantics. Options UI skeleton: tabbed categories, generic controls (toggle, slider, select, keybind placeholder), reset category to defaults, keyboard/gamepad navigable.
## Scope
- In: Schema, defaults, persistence + version migration, subscriptions
- In: Options menu shell with generic controls generated from schema metadata (label, help text, range)
- Out: Individual settings features (other e31 items)
- Out: Graphics presets implementation (e32-quality-presets)
## Notes
- Settings are per-browser, not per-save. Difficulty assists are settings too but read by sim via an injected config (never global reads from sim).

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0 — input actions, HUD vitals and inventory UI (all P0/m1) depend on it.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given stored settings with an unknown key and an out-of-range value, when loaded, then the unknown key is dropped, the value is clamped/defaulted and a warning is logged.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a subscriber to `audio.master`, when the value changes, then the callback fires once with the new value; unchanged sets do not fire.
- AC-3 [unit] Given stored settings at schema v1 and code at v2, when loaded, then the migration maps renamed keys and preserves user values.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the options menu, when a toggle is changed and the page reloaded, then the change persists.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given "Reset to defaults" in Camera, when confirmed, then only camera settings reset.
- AC-6 [integration] Given localStorage is unavailable, when the game starts, then defaults are used in-memory and no uncaught error occurs.

items.title: Let players remap keyboard, mouse and gamepad bindings
items.description:
## Why
Remapping is the single most-requested accessibility feature and a baseline expectation for PC action games.
## What
As a player, I want to rebind every action for keyboard/mouse and gamepad so that controls fit my hands and hardware.
Bindings screen lists actions from the action map with primary/secondary bindings per device; "press a key" capture with Esc to cancel; conflict detection with swap/replace prompt; reset per action and all; bindings persisted in settings.
## Scope
- In: Bindings UI over e02-input-actions API
- In: Conflict detection within the same context (e.g. exploration vs menu)
- Out: The action map itself (e02-input-actions)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given "Dodge" bound to Space, when rebound to Shift, then pressing Shift in the testbed triggers dodge and Space no longer does.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a new binding that conflicts with another action in the same context, when applied, then the user is prompted to swap or cancel and no silent duplicate exists.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an attempt to unbind the last binding for a required action (Pause/Menu), when applied, then it is refused with an explanation.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given capture mode, when Esc is pressed, then capture cancels without binding Esc.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given remapped bindings, when the page reloads, then bindings persist.

items.title: Offer hold vs toggle for sprint, crouch, block and aim
items.description:
## Why
Sustained key holds are a common motor-accessibility barrier; stealth and knight play involve long holds.
## What
As a player, I want to choose hold or toggle for sustained actions so that I do not need to keep keys pressed.
Per-action setting for sprint, crouch/sneak, block, aim/draw; toggle mode auto-releases on context change (e.g. entering dialogue).
## Scope
- In: Setting + input-layer adapter that converts toggle into a held state
- Out: Action definitions (e02-input-actions)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given crouch in toggle mode, when the key is pressed and released once, then the crouch command stays active until pressed again.
- AC-2 [unit] Given block toggled on, when dialogue opens, then block is released and does not resume after dialogue.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the setting changed mid-hold, when applied, then the action state resets to released without getting stuck.

items.title: Scale UI text 80–200% with readable defaults
items.description:
## Why
Books are central to the sorcerer fantasy and dialogue is text-only; unreadable text excludes players.
## What
As a player, I want to scale UI and book/dialogue text so that I can read comfortably at my screen distance.
Global UI scale and separate text size (80–200%), minimum default body size 18 px at 1080p, optional dyslexia-friendly font toggle, text background opacity for subtitles/dialogue.
## Scope
- In: CSS variable-driven scaling (or engine UI equivalent)
- In: Layout reflow at 200% without clipping
- Out: Captions content (e31-captions)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given text size 200%, when the dialogue, book reader and inventory screens are opened at 1280×720, then no text is clipped (Playwright overflow check on text nodes).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a stored value of 350%, when loaded, then it is clamped to 200%.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the dyslexia-friendly font toggled, when menus render, then the font family changes without reload.
- AC-4 [manual] Given default settings at 1080p on the reference machine, when a tester reads dialogue from 70 cm, then it is legible (body text ≥ 18 px).

items.title: Caption gameplay-critical sounds with direction indicators
items.description:
## Why
Stealth and combat depend on sound (footsteps, alerts, creature cues); deaf and hard-of-hearing players need that information visually.
## What
As a player, I want captions for important sounds with direction so that I can react to threats I cannot hear.
Sound events tagged `caption` (content data: text key, priority) display as short captions with an on-screen direction arrow relative to the camera; stacking/merging rules; size/background from text settings; toggle on/off.
## Scope
- In: Caption event pipeline from audio/sim noise events
- In: Direction indicator
- In: Content field `caption` on sound definitions
- Out: Audio engine (e28-audio-engine)
- Out: Noise event model (e09-sound-propagation)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a captioned noise event 90° to the player's right, when displayed, then the indicator points right (±15°).
- AC-2 [unit] Given 5 identical "footsteps" events within 2 s, when displayed, then they merge into one caption with a refreshed timer rather than 5 lines.
- AC-3 [unit] Given more than 4 simultaneous captions, when displayed, then the lowest-priority captions are dropped first.
- AC-4 [content] Given every sound definition flagged gameplay-critical, when validated, then it has a caption text key that exists in the strings table.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given captions enabled in the testbed, when a scripted guard alert sound plays, then its caption appears within 100 ms.

items.title: Add camera sensitivity, invert, FOV and auto-centre options
items.description:
## Why
Camera discomfort drives players away from third-person action games; control over it is basic comfort.
## What
As a player, I want to adjust camera sensitivity, inversion, FOV, distance and auto-centering so that the camera feels right to me.
Settings: mouse and stick sensitivity (separate X/Y), invert X/Y, FOV 60–100°, camera distance, auto-recentre on/off, lock-on switch sensitivity.
## Scope
- In: Settings wired to camera parameters via subscriptions
- Out: Camera implementation (e02-camera)
- Out: Shake/motion (e31-motion-comfort)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given invert Y enabled, when mouse moves up by 100 px, then camera pitch changes in the opposite direction to the default.
- AC-2 [unit] Given FOV set to 120 via storage tampering, when loaded, then it clamps to 100.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given sensitivity changed in the options menu, when returning to play, then the new sensitivity applies without reload.

items.title: Add motion comfort and photosensitivity safeguards
items.description:
## Why
Spectacular magic (constitution: magic should feel magical) must not trigger motion sickness or photosensitive seizures.
## What
As a player, I want to reduce camera shake, motion blur, head bob and flashes so that the game is comfortable and safe.
Settings: camera shake 0–100%, motion blur off, reduce flashing (caps full-screen luminance change frequency to ≤ 3 flashes/s and limits intensity), reduce screen effects (vignette/chromatic aberration). Honour `prefers-reduced-motion` as initial default.
## Scope
- In: Settings + a global "flash limiter" utility VFX must route through
- In: Default from prefers-reduced-motion
- Out: VFX system (e29-vfx-framework)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given reduce-flashing on, when VFX request 10 full-screen flashes within 1 s, then the limiter lets at most 3 through with intensity capped.
- AC-2 [unit] Given camera shake at 0%, when an impact requests shake, then camera offset remains zero.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` emulated on first launch, when settings initialise, then shake defaults to 0% and reduce-flashing to on.
