- AC-4 [manual] Given the spell/VFX showcase with reduce-flashing on, when reviewed against the Harding test guidance, then no sequence exceeds the flash threshold.

items.title: Ensure no gameplay information relies on colour alone
items.description:
## Why
Stealth awareness states, damage types and puzzle cues must be readable by colour-blind players (~8% of men).
## What
As a player, I want gameplay cues distinguishable without colour so that colour-blindness does not block me.
Audit and fix HUD/indicators to pair colour with shape/icon/pattern (alert states, element types, interactables), plus optional palette presets (deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia) for UI indicator colours.
## Scope
- In: UI indicator palette tokens + presets
- In: Design rule in docs/art/style-bible.md cross-reference
- Out: Full-screen colour filters (not planned; they degrade art)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given each awareness state indicator (Unaware→Combat), when rendered, then each has a distinct icon/shape independent of colour.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given each palette preset, when the HUD test page renders all indicators, then adjacent indicator colours differ by a contrast ratio ≥ 3:1 under simulated deficiency.
- AC-3 [manual] Given a colour-blind tester or simulator run through the testbed, when playing a stealth encounter, then all state changes are identified correctly.

items.title: Add per-bus volume sliders and mono audio
items.description:
## Why
Players must balance music against gameplay-critical sound; single-sided hearing requires mono.
## What
As a player, I want master/music/SFX/UI/ambience volume sliders and a mono toggle so that I can hear what matters.
Sliders map to audio engine buses (perceptual/log curve); mono downmix; mute when tab unfocused (optional).
## Scope
- In: Settings wired to e28 bus API
- Out: Mixer implementation (e28-audio-engine)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given music slider at 0, when the music bus gain is read, then it is 0 (silent) and SFX unaffected.
- AC-2 [unit] Given slider value 50%, when mapped, then gain follows the documented perceptual curve (≈ −10 dB ±1).
- AC-3 [integration] Given mono enabled, when a sound positioned hard left plays, then both output channels carry equal signal.

items.title: Provide difficulty presets and granular assists read by the sim
items.description:
## Why
Souls-like weight should not mean exclusion; granular assists let players keep the fantasy while tuning the challenge.
## What
As a player, I want difficulty presets and individual assists so that combat and stealth challenge suit me.
A sim-side `DifficultyConfig` (injected, part of save metadata): damage taken multiplier, parry/dodge timing window multiplier, enemy detection speed multiplier, stealth last-known-position search duration, puzzle hint availability, fall damage on/off. Presets Story/Adventurer/Veteran map to values; custom allowed. Changing mid-game allowed and recorded in local telemetry.
## Scope
- In: DifficultyConfig schema + injection into World
- In: Settings UI section
- In: Sim helper `difficulty.scale("damageTaken", x)` for systems to use
- Out: Systems applying the multipliers (each combat/stealth bead reads the config)
## Notes
- Related: e04 and e09 systems must read these multipliers; integration pass should add ACs there.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given preset Story, when resolved, then damageTaken=0.5, parryWindow=1.5, detectionSpeed=0.6 per the documented table.
- AC-2 [unit] Given damageTaken multiplier 0.5, when a 20-damage hit is scaled, then 10 damage results (integer rounding rule documented and tested).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a config value outside allowed bounds (e.g. parryWindow 10), when injected, then it is rejected by schema validation.
- AC-4 [unit] Given difficulty changed mid-session, when saved and reloaded, then the new config is restored and the change event was emitted once.
- AC-5 [integration] Given two replays identical except difficulty preset, when run, then state hashes differ (config is an input) and each replays deterministically.

items.title: Make every menu keyboard- and gamepad-operable with visible focus
items.description:
## Why
Menus that require a mouse block keyboard-only and gamepad players, and screen readers need labelled controls.
## What
As a player, I want to navigate all menus with keyboard or gamepad and see where focus is so that I never need a mouse.
Shared focus manager (spatial navigation), visible focus ring meeting 3:1 contrast, Esc/B back, ARIA labels/roles on DOM menus, axe-core checks in Playwright.
## Scope
- In: Focus manager, gamepad UI navigation, ARIA roles
- In: Playwright axe scan of each menu screen
- Out: In-game HUD screen reader support (post-MVP)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given each menu screen, when traversed with Tab/arrow keys only, then every interactive element is reachable and focus is always visible.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given each menu screen, when axe-core runs, then there are zero serious or critical violations.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given an emulated gamepad, when D-pad/A/B are used, then the same navigation works and B always returns to the previous screen.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given a modal dialog open, when Tab reaches its last control, then focus wraps inside the modal (focus trap).

items.title: Add gamepad deadzone, sensitivity curve and vibration settings
items.description:
## Why
Gamepad is second-class but supported; stick drift and vibration sensitivity vary by player and hardware.
## What
As a player, I want to tune stick deadzones, response curves and vibration so that my gamepad feels accurate.
Inner/outer deadzone per stick, response curve (linear/exponential), vibration intensity 0–100% (where Gamepad haptics are supported).
## Scope
- In: Settings + input-layer processing
- Out: Gamepad action mapping (e02-input-actions)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given inner deadzone 0.15, when stick magnitude is 0.1, then output is 0; at 1.0 output is 1.0 (rescaled).
- AC-2 [unit] Given vibration 0%, when a haptic request is made, then no vibration API call occurs.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a browser without `vibrationActuator`, when haptics are requested, then no error is thrown.

items.title: Audit MVP against Game Accessibility Guidelines basic tier
items.description:
## Why
Individual features do not guarantee an accessible whole; an audit before external playtests catches gaps.
## What
Walk through every GAG "basic" guideline (motor, cognitive, vision, hearing, speech, general) against the MVP build; record pass/fail/N-A with evidence in `docs/accessibility/audit-<date>.md`; file beads for each failure.
## Scope
- In: Audit doc, beads for findings
- Out: Fixing findings (separate beads)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the MVP build, when every GAG basic guideline is assessed, then the audit doc records a status and evidence for each.
- AC-2 [manual] Given any failing guideline, when the audit completes, then a bead exists for it with priority and a link from the audit doc.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the audit, when complete, then zero failures are left without a decision (fix, defer with reason, or N/A).

items.title: Build automated perf budget suite against the hardware baseline
items.description:
## Why
Performance regressions are cheapest to fix the day they land; budgets make "good browser performance" (constitution §10) enforceable.
## What
A Playwright-based perf suite (`pnpm perf`) with `perf-budgets.json` citing the contract baseline: frame time p50/p95 per scene and preset, time to first frame / playable, initial transfer size, JS heap after N minutes, long tasks count. Two execution modes:
  1. **CI mode** (GPU-less runners): enforces deterministic-ish budgets — transfer size, bundle size, heap, load time under network throttling (50 Mbps), long tasks > 200 ms, and relative regression of software-rendered frame time vs main (± 15%) as a warning.
  2. **Reference mode** (`pnpm perf:ref`, manual on the M1 Pro reference machine): enforces absolute frame-time budgets and writes `perf/results/<date>-<sha>.json`; committed results feed the trend chart.
Includes a baseline stress scene in the greybox kit (N moving physics props + lights).
## Scope
- In: Perf harness (frame-time sampling via rAF + PerformanceObserver long tasks, CDP heap), budget file, reporters (JSON + job summary)
- In: CI job `perf-budget`
- In: Baseline stress scene `perf-baseline`
- Out: Creature/combat stress scene (e32-combat-stress-scene)
- Out: Cross-browser runs (e32-browser-matrix)
## Notes
- Budget numbers come only from backlog-contract §1 Hardware baseline; stories cite them rather than inventing new ones.
- Frame-time sampling excludes the first 3 s (warm-up) and uses ≥ 1,800 frames.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the `perf-baseline` scene in reference mode on the reference machine (High, 1440p-equivalent), when measured over 1,800 frames, then p95 frame time ≤ 16.7 ms or the run fails with a per-metric report.
- AC-2 [integration] Given CI mode, when initial transfer size exceeds 50 MB or throttled load-to-playable exceeds 10 s, then `perf-budget` fails naming the metric and delta vs budget.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a samples array, when percentiles are computed, then p50/p95/p99 match a committed reference implementation, and fewer than 300 samples yields an "insufficient samples" failure rather than a pass.
- AC-4 [integration] Given heap after 5 minutes idle in the testbed exceeds 1.5 GB, when measured, then the suite fails.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a PR whose software-rendered frame time regresses > 15% vs main, when CI runs, then a warning annotation appears (non-blocking).
- AC-6 [unit] Given `perf-budgets.json` with a budget lacking a `source` field citing the baseline, when validated, then it fails.

items.title: Benchmark sim tick cost in CI with regression alerts
items.description:
## Why
The sim runs every tick regardless of GPU; its cost is measurable headlessly and must stay well inside the frame budget.
## What
`vitest bench` suites for representative sim loads (500 entities with propagation, 30 AI agents perceiving, 200 physics props) with a budget: mean tick ≤ 4 ms in Node on CI hardware. CI compares against main baseline artifact and fails on > 25% regression.
## Scope
- In: Bench suites, baseline artifact, comparison script
- Out: Frame-time budgets (e32-perf-budgets)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the "full-load" bench, when run in CI, then mean tick ≤ 4 ms and p99 ≤ 8 ms.
- AC-2 [unit] Given baseline 2.0 ms and PR 2.6 ms, when compared, then the check fails (30% > 25%); at 2.4 ms it passes.
- AC-3 [unit] Given no baseline available, when compared, then it records a new baseline and passes with a warning.

items.title: Enforce JS bundle and asset size budgets per PR
items.description:
## Why
Initial download ≤ 50 MB and load ≤ 10 s are easiest to protect byte by byte at PR time.
## What
size-limit (or custom script) over `dist/`: initial JS ≤ 1.5 MB gz, total initial payload ≤ 50 MB, per-asset caps by type (texture ≤ 4 MB, audio loop ≤ 3 MB). PR comment/job summary shows delta vs main; dev tools must not appear in the production bundle.
## Scope
- In: Size budget config + check job
- In: Assertion that `src/tools/**` modules are absent from prod chunks
- Out: Asset compression pipeline (e32-asset-loading)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a PR increasing initial JS beyond 1.5 MB gz, when CI runs, then the size check fails showing the delta.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a production build, when chunk contents are inspected, then no module from `src/tools/` is present.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a single texture of 6 MB added, when checked, then it fails naming the file and the 4 MB cap.

items.title: Run smoke suite on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit in CI
items.description:
## Why
Target browsers are current Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari; engine-specific breakage must be caught before players see it.
## What
Playwright projects for chromium, firefox, webkit running the boot + testbed smoke specs in CI (chromium required per-PR; firefox/webkit required on main and nightly, optional per-PR label `full-matrix`). Known-difference allowlist per browser with bead references.
## Scope
- In: Playwright project matrix, CI job(s), docs of manual Edge/Safari checks
- Out: Mobile browsers (mw-e36)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the smoke suite, when run on chromium, firefox and webkit, then the testbed boots with zero console errors on all three.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a nightly run failing on webkit only, when complete, then a GitHub issue is opened/updated with the failing spec and trace artifact.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a known-difference allowlist entry without a bead id, when validated, then CI fails.

items.title: Detect GPU/browser capabilities and pick a safe default preset
items.description:
## Why
First impressions matter: a low-end laptop should start on Low, and unsupported browsers need a clear message.
## What
On boot detect WebGL2 (and WebGPU if the ADR uses it), WASM + SIMD, max texture size, `deviceMemory`, `hardwareConcurrency`, renderer string (where exposed); choose default preset (High/Low) on first launch; show an unsupported screen listing what is missing; log capabilities to local telemetry.
## Scope
- In: Capability probe, preset heuristic table, unsupported screen
- Out: Dynamic resolution at runtime (e32-quality-presets)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given capabilities {deviceMemory: 4, renderer contains "Intel"}, when the heuristic runs, then Low is chosen; given an Apple M1 Pro renderer string, then High.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given WebGL2 unavailable (init-script override), when loaded, then the unsupported screen names WebGL2 and links to browser help.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the renderer string is masked/unavailable, when the heuristic runs, then it falls back to deviceMemory/cores and never throws.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the player has already chosen a preset, when the game boots again, then detection does not override it.

items.title: Implement Low/High graphics presets and dynamic resolution
items.description:
## Why
The baseline defines two presets; they must actually hit 60 fps on their target hardware.
## What
As a player, I want Low/High presets plus individual toggles and optional dynamic resolution so that the game runs smoothly on my machine.
Preset controls render scale, shadow resolution/cascades, max dynamic lights, post-processing, particle density, LOD bias, draw distance. Dynamic resolution adjusts render scale between 50–100% to hold a frame-time target, with hysteresis.
## Scope
- In: Preset table, settings UI section, dynamic resolution controller (pure logic unit-tested)
- Out: Asset LODs creation (art epics)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given frame times consistently 20 ms with target 16.7 ms, when the controller updates, then render scale steps down by ≤ 10% per second and never below 50%.
- AC-2 [unit] Given frame times oscillating around target ±0.5 ms, when the controller runs, then scale changes at most once per 2 s (hysteresis).
- AC-3 [perf] Given the combat stress scene on Low at 1080p on an Iris Xe / base M1 class machine, when measured, then p50 ≥ 60 fps and p95 frame time ≤ 33.3 ms.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given a preset switch at runtime, when applied, then it takes effect within 1 s without reload or console errors.

items.title: Stream and compress assets with a progress-reporting loader
items.description:
## Why
Load to playable ≤ 10 s requires compressed assets and loading only what the current area needs.
## What
Asset manifest generated at build (id → hashed URL, size, area tags); area-based preloading with priority; texture compression (KTX2/Basis), mesh compression (meshopt or Draco per ADR), audio as Opus/AAC with fallback; loading screen showing real progress; failed-fetch retry with backoff.
## Scope
- In: Manifest build step, loader with priorities/retries, compression tooling scripts
- In: Loading screen progress
- Out: Service-worker/HTTP caching (e32-asset-caching)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given a cold load at 50 Mbps throttling in CI mode, when Briar-Glen-equivalent testbed area loads, then playable ≤ 10 s.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a fetch failing twice then succeeding, when loading, then the loader retries with backoff and completes; after 3 failures it surfaces a retry UI.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the manifest, when an asset id is missing, then a typed error names the id at build time (build fails).
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the loading screen, when assets load, then the progress bar increases monotonically from 0 to 100%.

items.title: Cache hashed assets for warm reload ≤ 3 s
items.description:
## Why
Warm reload ≤ 3 s keeps the death/retry and playtest loops snappy.
## What
Immutable caching for content-hashed assets (Pages headers are limited, so add a service worker with cache-first for hashed URLs and network-first for index.html); versioned cache names with cleanup of old versions on activate; opt-out via `?nosw`.
## Scope
- In: Service worker (Workbox or hand-rolled), update flow ("new version available — reload")
- Out: Offline play guarantee (nice side effect, not a goal)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given a previously loaded build, when the page is reloaded, then load to playable ≤ 3 s on the reference machine.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given a new deployment, when the page loads, then the old cache version is deleted after activation and a "new version available" prompt appears.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given `?nosw`, when loaded, then no service worker is registered and existing ones are unregistered.

items.title: Eliminate frame hitches from GC, shader compilation and long tasks
items.description:
## Why
Stable frame pacing matters more than average fps for combat feel (parry timing).
## What
Detect and fix hitch sources: shader/pipeline pre-warm during loading, object pooling for projectiles/particles/events on hot paths, long-task detection in dev overlay, allocation audit of the sim tick (target near-zero allocations per tick).
## Scope
- In: Shader pre-warm, pools, allocation test for sim tick
- Out: Perf HUD (e32-perf-hud)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the combat stress scene for 60 s on the reference machine, when measured, then frames > 33 ms number ≤ 3 and none > 50 ms after warm-up.
- AC-2 [unit] Given 1,000 steady-state sim ticks, when heap allocations are measured in Node (`--expose-gc` heap delta), then growth ≤ 64 KB.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the first cast of each VFX type after loading, when measured, then no frame exceeds 33 ms (pre-warm effective).

items.title: Show a dev perf HUD with frame graph, draw calls and heap
items.description:
## Why
Developers need to see performance cost while building content, not after CI complains.
## What
As a developer, I want an overlay showing fps, frame-time graph (last 240 frames), sim tick ms, draw calls, triangles, textures/geometries count and JS heap so that I can spot regressions immediately.
Toggle via debug console or F3; dev builds only.
## Scope
- In: Overlay, renderer stats adapter
- Out: Automated budgets (e32-perf-budgets)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a dev build, when F3 is pressed, then the HUD shows fps, frame-time graph, sim ms, draw calls and heap values that update each frame.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a production build, when F3 is pressed, then nothing happens and HUD code is absent from the bundle.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `performance.memory` is unavailable (Firefox/Safari), when the HUD renders, then heap shows "n/a" without errors.

items.title: Recover gracefully from WebGL/GPU context loss
items.description:
## Why
GPU resets happen (driver updates, sleep/wake); losing a session to a black screen is avoidable.
## What
Handle `webglcontextlost`/`restored` (or WebGPU device lost): pause sim, show overlay, rebuild GPU resources from the asset cache on restore, resume; if restore fails within 10 s, autosave (if safe) and offer reload.
## Scope
- In: Context-loss handler, resource rebuild path
- Out: Save logic (e30-autosave)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given `WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext()` then `restoreContext()`, when triggered in the testbed, then rendering resumes within 5 s with the same sim state hash as before loss.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the context is never restored, when 10 s pass, then an autosave is attempted and a reload prompt appears.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given loss during loading, when restored, then loading completes without duplicate resources or errors.

items.title: Detect memory leaks across repeated scene loads
items.description:
## Why
Area transitions and reloads after death repeat hundreds of times per session; leaks compound into crashes.
## What
Playwright test (Chromium, CDP heap) loads/unloads testbed scenes and save/load cycles 20 times, forcing GC, and asserts heap growth and GPU resource counts stay bounded.
## Scope
- In: Leak test spec, renderer resource counters
- Out: Fixing specific leaks (bug beads)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given 20 scene load/unload cycles, when heap is sampled after forced GC, then growth from cycle 2 to cycle 20 ≤ 5%.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given 20 save/load cycles, when renderer geometry/texture counts are read, then they return to the cycle-2 value (±2).
- AC-3 [integration] Given a deliberately leaking fixture, when the test runs, then it fails (test proves it can detect leaks).

items.title: Add combat stress scene with 12 creatures and heavy VFX
items.description:
## Why
The worst case — a chaotic fight with spells flying — is what players remember; budgets must be measured there.
## What
Scene `perf-combat` in the greybox kit: 12 active creatures in combat AI, 4 simultaneous spell effects, 30 physics props, fire propagation active, 8 dynamic lights. Scripted deterministic camera path and input replay so measurements are repeatable. Added to both perf modes.
## Scope
- In: Scene data, scripted replay, perf-budgets.json entries
- Out: Creature content (mw-e13)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given `perf-combat` on the reference machine (High), when measured over 1,800 frames, then p95 frame time ≤ 16.7 ms.
- AC-2 [perf] Given `perf-combat` on Low at 1080p on the low-tier class machine, when measured, then worst-case frames stay ≥ 30 fps (p99 ≤ 33.3 ms).
- AC-3 [unit] Given the scripted replay, when run twice, then sim state hashes match (repeatable measurement).

items.title: Run and record a full perf pass on reference and low-tier machines
items.description:
## Why
Absolute frame-time budgets cannot run on GPU-less CI; a documented manual pass before playtests closes the loop.
## What
Write `docs/perf/runbook.md` (machine prep, browser versions, `pnpm perf:ref` steps) and execute it on the reference machine and a low-tier machine across Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari; commit results to `perf/results/`; file beads for any budget misses.
## Scope
- In: Runbook doc, committed results, beads for misses
- Out: Fixes (separate beads)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the runbook, when executed on the reference machine in all 4 browsers, then results files are committed with browser/OS versions.
- AC-2 [perf] Given the results, when compared to the baseline, then every budget passes or has a filed bead with owner and priority.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the low-tier machine run, when complete, then Low preset results are recorded for `perf-baseline` and `perf-combat`.

items.title: Add in-game debug console with commands, cheats and spawners
items.description:
## Why
Fast content creation and debugging (constitution §10) need a way to poke the running game without editing code.
## What
As a developer, I want a toggleable console with typed commands so that I can spawn, teleport, cheat and inspect instantly.
Backtick toggles an overlay console (dev builds and `?debug=1` on playtest builds); command registry (`registerCommand({name, args schema, run})`) with autocomplete, history (persisted), help. Built-ins: `help`, `spawn <contentId> [count]`, `give <itemId> [n]`, `god`, `noclip`, `kill`, `tp <x y z|bookmark>`, `timescale <n>`, `scene <id>`, `set <setting> <value>`, `seed`. Commands that mutate sim state go through the sim command queue (deterministic, recorded in replays).
## Scope
- In: Console UI, registry, parser with zod arg validation, autocomplete against content ids
- In: Built-in commands
- In: Production stripping (dynamic import behind build flag)
- Out: Entity inspector (e33-entity-inspector)
- Out: Domain-specific commands (each system registers its own)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given `spawn testprop-crate 3`, when executed, then 3 crate entities exist in the sim next tick and the command is present in the replay input log.
- AC-2 [unit] Given `spawn does-not-exist`, when executed, then the console prints "unknown content id" with the 3 closest matches and the sim is unchanged.
- AC-3 [unit] Given `give` with a non-numeric count, when executed, then argument validation fails with usage help.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given a dev build, when backtick is pressed, then the console opens, captures keyboard input (player does not move) and Esc/backtick closes it.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a production build without `?debug=1`, when backtick is pressed, then nothing opens and console modules are absent from the main bundle.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given typing `sp` + Tab, when autocomplete runs, then it completes to `spawn`.

items.title: Pause, slow-motion and frame-step the simulation
items.description:
## Why
Tuning parry windows and debugging propagation needs time slowed or stepped one tick at a time.
## What
As a developer, I want to pause, change timescale (0.1×–4×) and step single ticks so that I can inspect fast interactions.
Implemented in the game loop (sim steps at fixed dt; timescale changes how many steps per real second), so determinism is preserved.
## Scope
- In: Loop timescale, pause, step; console commands and hotkeys (dev)
- Out: Replay scrubbing (possible follow-up)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given timescale 0.5, when 1 real second passes at 60 Hz, then 30 sim steps occur.
- AC-2 [unit] Given paused, when "step" is invoked 3 times, then exactly 3 ticks advance.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a session played at mixed timescales and recorded, when replayed at 1×, then the final state hash matches.

items.title: Inspect and edit entity components live
items.description:
## Why
Systemic bugs ("why didn't the rope burn?") are solved by seeing the properties involved.
## What
As a developer, I want to click an entity and see/edit its components live so that I can debug systemic interactions.
Pick via raycast (or list/search), panel showing components with schema-driven editors (number, bool, enum, vector), edits applied through a `debug.setComponent` sim command (recorded), highlight selected entity.
## Scope
- In: Picker, inspector panel, edit command
- Out: World overlays (e33-world-overlays)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the testbed, when a crate is clicked in inspect mode, then its components (e.g. Position, Physics) are listed with current values updating live.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an edit setting a numeric field to a string, when applied, then schema validation rejects it and the sim is unchanged.
- AC-3 [integration] Given an edit to `flammable=true`, when recorded and replayed, then the replay reproduces the edited state.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the selected entity is destroyed, when the next frame renders, then the panel shows "entity destroyed" instead of throwing.

items.title: Add `pnpm content:check` validator with cross-reference report
items.description:
## Why
Designers need fast, readable validation of all content before committing; CI needs the same check.
## What
CLI wrapping the content pipeline: validates all content types, cross-references (loot tables → items, spawns → creatures, dialogue → quests), orphan detection (defined but never referenced), string-table key existence; human-readable output with file:line, `--json` for CI annotations; runs in CI job `content`.
## Scope
- In: CLI, CI job, GitHub annotation formatter
- Out: Schemas themselves (owned by respective epics)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given all committed content, when `pnpm content:check` runs, then it exits 0 in ≤ 10 s.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a loot table referencing a missing item, when checked, then it exits non-zero printing the file, JSON path and missing id.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an item defined but never referenced by any loot table, shop or placement, when checked with `--orphans`, then it is listed as a warning (not an error).
- AC-4 [integration] Given `--json`, when run in CI with an error, then a GitHub annotation appears on the offending file.

items.title: Scaffold new content entries with a test stub via CLI
items.description:
## Why
Every content entry must have a test (contract §3); scaffolding makes the right thing the easy thing.
## What
`pnpm new <type> <id>` creates `content/<type>/<id>.json` from a per-type template (valid defaults) and a test stub `test/content/<type>/<id>.test.ts` that exercises the entry via `describeContent`; refuses duplicate ids; validates id format (kebab-case).
## Scope
- In: CLI, per-type templates registered alongside schemas
- Out: GUI editors (not planned for MVP)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given `pnpm new testprop lantern`, when run, then the JSON and test stub are created, `pnpm content:check` passes and the new test runs green.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an id that already exists, when run, then it exits non-zero without overwriting.
- AC-3 [unit] Given id `Big Lantern`, when run, then it rejects with a kebab-case suggestion `big-lantern`.

items.title: Hot-reload content JSON into the running game
items.description:
## Why
Tuning spells and creatures by editing JSON and seeing the change in under a second is the core of fast content iteration.
## What
As a designer, I want edits to content files to apply to the running game without restart so that tuning is instant.
Vite HMR for `content/**` → re-validate the changed file → swap catalogue entry → notify systems (`content.on("changed", id)`) which refresh live instances where safe (e.g. spell damage, creature speed); invalid edits keep the old version and show an overlay error.
## Scope
- In: HMR handler, catalogue swap, change notifications, error overlay
- Out: Production (dev only)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the dev server and testbed running, when a testprop JSON field is edited, then the change is visible in-game within 1 s without page reload.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given an edit introducing a schema error, when saved, then an overlay shows the error with file and path and the game keeps running on the previous valid data.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a hot-swapped entry, when the content hash is recomputed, then it changes and the replay recorder marks the recording as content-modified.

items.title: Add named teleport bookmarks and dev state snapshots
items.description:
## Why
Reaching the room you are working on in seconds, in the right world state, removes most iteration friction.
## What
As a developer, I want named bookmarks and instant dev snapshots so that I can jump to a place and state repeatedly.
Bookmarks as content (`content/dev/bookmarks.json`) + console `tp <name>`; `snap save <name>` / `snap load <name>` store full save envelopes in a dev IndexedDB store; URL `?snap=<name>` boots into a snapshot.
## Scope
- In: Bookmarks, snapshot commands, URL param
- Out: Player save slots (e30-save-slots)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given bookmark `arena-center`, when `tp arena-center` runs, then the player is placed there next tick.
- AC-2 [integration] Given `snap save a` then changes then `snap load a`, when compared, then the state hash equals the snapshot's.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a snapshot from an older save schema, when loaded, then save migrations apply; if they fail, a clear error is shown.

items.title: Capture a reproducible bug report with one keypress
items.description:
## Why
Emergent systems create hard-to-reproduce bugs; a deterministic replay of the last minutes turns "it happened once" into a failing test.
## What
As a developer or playtester, I want to press F9-dev (configurable) to save a bug bundle so that the exact situation can be replayed.
The game continuously keeps a rolling buffer: a save snapshot every 60 s plus input commands since. Capture writes `bug-<timestamp>.mwbug` (snapshot + inputs + build SHA + content hash + settings + recent console/errors + screenshot + optional note). `?bug=<file>` or drag-drop loads and replays it; `pnpm bug:test <file>` converts it into a golden replay test.
## Scope
- In: Rolling buffer, bundle format (zod), loader, conversion to test
- Out: Telemetry export bundles (e34-playtest-export) — reuse format pieces
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given 3 minutes of play then capture, when the bundle is replayed on a fresh load of the same build, then the final state hash equals the captured final hash.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a bundle from a different build SHA, when loaded, then the user is warned that replay may diverge and divergence is reported at the first checkpoint mismatch.
- AC-3 [perf] Given the rolling buffer active, when measured in the testbed, then added cost is ≤ 0.2 ms per frame and memory ≤ 20 MB.
- AC-4 [integration] Given `pnpm bug:test`, when run on a bundle, then a replay test file is generated that passes.

items.title: Visualize perception cones, alert states and noise events
items.description:
## Why
Stealth that feels fair requires designers to see exactly what creatures perceive and why.
## What
As a designer, I want overlays for sight cones, hearing radii, current alert state, last-known-position markers, search paths and noise events so that I can tune stealth encounters.
Overlay toggles per category; reads sim data only (no sim changes).
## Scope
- In: Overlay renderer for AI/perception data, toggles via console
- Out: AI logic (mw-e11)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a guard in the testbed with the overlay on, when the player is in the sight cone, then the cone renders and the guard's alert label changes as the state progresses.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given a noise event, when emitted, then an expanding ring shows its propagated radius for 1 s.
- AC-3 [integration] Given overlays toggled on vs off, when the same replay runs, then sim state hashes are identical (overlay is read-only).

items.title: Visualize light levels, element propagation and trigger volumes
items.description:
## Why
The systemic world (fire, water, light, triggers) is invisible data until visualized; debugging emergent interactions depends on it.
## What
As a designer, I want heatmap overlays for light level, temperature/fire, wetness/electricity and trigger volume outlines so that I can see why systemic interactions do or do not happen.
Grid-sampled overlays from sim queries; property-tag filter ("show all flammable").
## Scope
- In: Light field heatmap, element overlays, trigger volume wireframes, property filter
- Out: The systems themselves (mw-e03)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the light overlay in a room with one torch, when shown, then sampled values decrease with distance from the torch.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the property filter `flammable`, when enabled, then exactly the entities with that tag are highlighted.
- AC-3 [integration] Given overlays on vs off, when the same replay runs, then state hashes are identical.

items.title: Create a spell sandbox scene with live parameter tuning
items.description:
## Why
Magic must feel magical; designers need a playground to cast every spell against every material and creature.
## What
As a designer, I want a sandbox with material stations (water, oil, wood, rope, metal) and dummies where I can cast any spell and tweak its parameters live so that I can find surprising combinations.
Scene `sandbox-spells`, console `learnall`, `cast <spellId>`, parameter panel bound to hot-reloadable spell data.
## Scope
- In: Sandbox scene, commands, parameter panel
- Out: Spell content (mw-e08)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given `?scene=sandbox-spells` and `learnall`, when opened, then every spell in content is castable from a list.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given a spell's radius changed in the panel, when cast again, then the new radius applies without reload.
- AC-3 [content] Given the sandbox scene, when validated, then it contains at least one entity for every property tag defined in e03-world-properties.

items.title: Create a creature arena to spawn and pit creatures
items.description:
## Why
Creatures are creatures, not target dummies; their behaviours and relationships need a place to be observed.
## What
As a designer, I want an arena where I can spawn any creature with chosen disposition/faction and watch interactions so that I can tune behaviours.
Scene `sandbox-creatures`, commands `spawn <creature> --faction --disposition`, `ai freeze/unfreeze`, `faction set`.
## Scope
- In: Arena scene, commands
- Out: AI implementation (mw-e11/mw-e12)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the arena, when `spawn goblin-grunt --disposition hostile` and `spawn wolf --disposition neutral` run, then both spawn with those dispositions visible in the inspector.
- AC-2 [unit] Given `ai freeze`, when ticks advance, then frozen creatures' AI systems do not update while physics still does.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature id with invalid disposition, when spawned, then validation fails with allowed values listed.

items.title: Preview dialogue graphs and edit quest/world state in-game
items.description:
## Why
Branching quests with multiple resolutions are untestable by playing through every path manually.
## What
As a narrative designer, I want a dialogue previewer and a quest/world-fact editor so that I can test any branch instantly.
Dialogue previewer runs a dialogue graph standalone with editable condition inputs (disposition, facts, inventory). Quest panel lists quests, states, objectives; set state/fact via recorded debug commands. Graph lint: unreachable nodes, dead ends without exit.
## Scope
- In: Previewer panel, quest/fact panel, graph lint in content:check
- Out: Runtimes (e22-dialogue-runtime, e23-quest-runtime, e27-world-state-store)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a dialogue id, when opened in the previewer with disposition=friendly, then only nodes whose conditions pass are selectable.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a dialogue graph with an unreachable node, when linted, then content:check reports the node id.
- AC-3 [integration] Given `quest set <id> <state>`, when executed, then dependent world facts update and the change is recorded in the replay.

items.title: Simulate loot tables and report drop distributions
items.description:
## Why
Exploration should produce interesting discoveries; designers need to see actual distributions, not guess from weights.
## What
CLI `pnpm loot:sim <tableId> --rolls 10000 --seed 1` prints item frequencies, expected gold, and flags items with 0 drops or duplicates of "unique" items; also available as console command.
## Scope
- In: CLI + console command using sim loot roller with seeded RNG
- Out: Loot runtime (e18-loot-tables)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a table with weights 1:3, when 10,000 rolls simulate with seed 1, then frequencies are 25% ± 1.5% and 75% ± 1.5% and the output is identical across runs.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a unique item that can drop twice in one roll, when simulated, then it is flagged.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an unknown table id, when run, then it exits non-zero listing close matches.

items.title: Define local-first telemetry event schema, store and export
items.description:
## Why
Measuring deaths, abandonments and spell usage guides design — but this is a free game and players' privacy comes first.
## What
Add `src/game/telemetry`: a zod-typed event catalogue (`{type, v, sessionId (random per session), tick, simTimeMs, area, payload}`), a typed `emit()` API, a bounded local ring buffer in IndexedDB (max 50k events / 20 MB, oldest dropped), and export to NDJSON (gzip). No network code in this item. Events are only recorded if telemetry is enabled (e34-consent) except a small in-memory buffer used for bug reports.
## Scope
- In: Event catalogue, emitter, IndexedDB store, export, clear-all
- In: Schema rule: no free-text string fields except enumerated ids (enforced by schema test)
- Out: Consent UI (e34-consent)
- Out: Specific gameplay events (e34-gameplay-events)
- Out: Any upload (e34-opt-in-upload)
## Notes
- Session id is random, not derived from device; no user id, no IP, no fingerprinting data (UA only as coarse browser family + version).

**Integration note:** Moved to m2 — e04-skeleton-fun-validation (m2) consumes it.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an event missing a required payload field, when emitted, then it is dropped and a dev-only warning logged (never throws into gameplay).
- AC-2 [unit] Given the ring buffer at capacity, when a new event is stored, then the oldest is evicted and count stays at the cap.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the event catalogue, when a schema-lint test inspects it, then no event has an unconstrained free-text string field.
- AC-4 [integration] Given 1,000 stored events, when exported, then the NDJSON file has 1,000 valid lines that re-parse against the schema.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given telemetry disabled (default), when playing for 2 minutes, then nothing is written to the telemetry IndexedDB store and zero network requests carry telemetry.

items.title: Add opt-in telemetry consent, privacy notice and data controls
items.description:
## Why
Privacy-first: players must knowingly opt in, see exactly what is recorded, and delete it anytime.
## What
As a player, I want to choose whether gameplay statistics are recorded, see what is recorded and delete it so that I stay in control.
Off by default. First-launch (or playtest-mode) prompt explains local-first recording; settings toggle; "View my data" (event counts by type + sample), "Export", "Delete all". `docs/privacy.md` published with the site.
## Scope
- In: Consent prompt, settings controls, privacy doc
- Out: Upload consent (separate, e34-opt-in-upload)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a fresh profile, when the game starts, then telemetry is off until the player explicitly opts in.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given telemetry on with stored events, when "Delete all" is confirmed, then the store is empty and the counts show 0.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the player opts out after opting in, when playing further, then no new events are stored.
- AC-4 [manual] Given docs/privacy.md, when reviewed, then it lists every event type and field recorded and states nothing leaves the device without a separate explicit action.

items.title: Emit core gameplay events: deaths, encounters, spells, puzzles
items.description:
## Why
E34 outcome names these signals explicitly: deaths, abandoned encounters, spell usage and puzzle completion.
## What
Instrument: `session_start/end` (class, build), `death` (cause type, killer content id, area, position bucketed to 2 m), `encounter_start/complete/abandon` (encounter id, duration, resolution: combat/stealth/social/avoid), `spell_cast` (spell id, target type, outcome tags), `puzzle_start/solve/abandon` (puzzle id, solution path id), `ability_used` (class verb id), `setting_changed` (difficulty/assist ids only), `item_acquired` (source: loot/shop/steal).
## Scope
- In: Event definitions + emit points in game glue listening to sim events
- In: Encounter/puzzle id conventions in content
- Out: Analysis (e34-analysis-scripts)
## Notes
- Emit from game layer listening to the sim event bus — never call telemetry from src/sim.
- Abandon = left encounter/puzzle volume for > 60 s without resolution (configurable).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the testbed with a scripted fight replay ending in player death, when run, then exactly one `death` event is recorded with cause, killer id and 2 m-bucketed position.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player leaves an encounter volume for 61 s unresolved, when evaluated, then `encounter_abandon` is emitted once; returning at 59 s emits nothing.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a puzzle solved via an alternative solution path, when emitted, then `puzzle_solve.solutionPath` identifies that path id.
- AC-4 [unit] Given telemetry disabled, when sim events fire, then emitters short-circuit without allocation-heavy work (≤ 0.01 ms per event measured).

items.title: Capture uncaught errors locally for playtest bundles
items.description:
## Why
Playtesters rarely report console errors; capturing them locally makes crashes diagnosable without third-party services.
## What
Global `error`/`unhandledrejection` handlers record `{message, stack (sanitized of URLs query strings), buildSha, area, tick}` into a small local error log (always on, local only, max 200 entries) shown in the bug/feedback bundle and "View my data".
## Scope
- In: Handlers, sanitizer, local log
- Out: Remote error reporting services (not used)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a thrown error with a stack containing `?token=abc`, when sanitized, then query strings are stripped.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given an unhandled promise rejection, when it occurs, then an entry is logged and the game continues running.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 250 errors, when logged, then only the latest 200 are kept and repeated identical errors are counted rather than duplicated.

items.title: Add an in-game feedback hotkey capturing context and a note
items.description:
## Why
Players' moments of delight or confusion are best captured in the moment, tied to where and when they happened.
## What
As a playtester, I want to press a key, type a quick note and tag it (bug / confusing / fun / idea) so that my feedback carries its context.
Captures screenshot, area, position, tick, recent 60 s of events (if enabled), optional bug bundle (e33-replay-bug-capture); stored locally and included in the playtest export.
## Scope
- In: Feedback overlay, local storage, inclusion in export
- Out: Uploading (e34-opt-in-upload)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the feedback key pressed, when the overlay opens, then the game pauses and resumes on close.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given a submitted note tagged "fun", when exported, then the bundle contains the note, tag, screenshot and area/tick.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a note longer than 2,000 characters, when submitted, then it is truncated with an indicator.

items.title: Export a single playtest bundle file for testers to send
items.description:
## Why
External testers need a one-click way to share everything useful, without accounts or servers.
## What
As a playtester, I want one "Export playtest data" button producing one file so that sending results to the team is trivial.
Bundle `.mwplay` (zip): telemetry NDJSON, error log, feedback notes + screenshots, settings, build SHA, capability summary, optional latest save and bug bundles. Shows file size and a contents preview before saving.
## Scope
- In: Bundle writer (zip in browser), preview dialog
- Out: Analysis (e34-analysis-scripts)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a session with events, feedback and errors, when exported, then the bundle contains each component and a manifest listing them with counts.
- AC-2 [integration] Given telemetry disabled, when exported, then the bundle omits telemetry and the manifest says so.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the bundle manifest schema, when an exported bundle is parsed by the analysis tooling, then it validates.

items.title: Aggregate playtest bundles into a death heatmap and usage report
items.description:
## Why
Telemetry only matters if it turns into decisions; the team needs a quick report per playtest round.
## What
`pnpm playtest:report <dir>` reads N `.mwplay` bundles and writes a single-file HTML report: death heatmap over top-down area maps, encounter resolution breakdown (combat/stealth/social/avoid) and abandonment rates, spell usage frequency per class, puzzle solve rates and solution-path distribution, session length, feedback notes by tag with screenshots.
## Scope
- In: Node aggregation (100% covered pure functions), HTML report generator
- In: Top-down map images generated from greybox scenes
- Out: Qualitative observation notes (e35 protocol)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 3 fixture bundles with known deaths, when aggregated, then per-area death counts and heatmap bins match expected values.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a corrupt or wrong-version bundle among valid ones, when processed, then it is skipped with a warning and the report still builds.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the report, when opened in Playwright offline, then it renders all sections with zero console errors.
- AC-4 [unit] Given encounters resolved 5 combat / 3 stealth / 2 avoided, when aggregated, then the breakdown shows 50/30/20%.

items.title: Offer optional, explicit upload of a playtest bundle
items.description:
## Why
Manual file sending adds friction for remote testers; an explicit upload button can help, but only with separate consent.
## What
As a playtester, I want to optionally upload my bundle with one click after reviewing it so that I do not have to email files.
Separate consent per upload (preview + "Upload" button), minimal endpoint (e.g. serverless function writing to private storage) with size limit and rate limiting, no cookies, delete-by-receipt-code.
## Scope
- In: Upload UI, endpoint spec, ADR on hosting choice
- Out: Automatic/background upload (never)
## Notes
- Deferred post-MVP: file export covers MVP playtests. Requires secret handling for the endpoint — no secrets in the repo.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the upload dialog, when the player does not press Upload, then zero network requests leave the page.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a bundle > 25 MB, when upload is attempted, then it is refused client-side with a message.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a successful upload, when complete, then a receipt code is shown that can be used to request deletion.

items.title: Pre-register measurable fun hypotheses for MVP validation
items.description:
## Why
Fun validation is only honest if success criteria are written before playtests, not rationalized after.
## What
Write `docs/playtesting/fun-hypotheses.md`: per pillar (combat intrinsically fun, magic feels magical, stealth satisfying, world rewards curiosity, classes change possibilities) define hypotheses with measures and thresholds, e.g. "≥ 70% of testers rate fighting a skeleton ≥ 4/5 with loot/XP disabled", "≥ 3 self-reported 'Wait… I can do that?' moments per hour (median)", "≥ 25% of dungeon encounters resolved without combat across thief players", "≥ 60% of sorcerers try a spell on the environment unprompted within 15 min". Includes go/no-go rule.
## Scope
- In: Hypotheses doc with measures, thresholds, data source (survey/observation/telemetry)
- Out: Running tests (later e35 items)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the doc, when reviewed, then each constitution design pillar has ≥ 1 hypothesis with a numeric threshold and named data source.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the doc, when merged, then it defines an explicit go/no-go rule (e.g. which hypotheses must pass).
- AC-3 [manual] Given a hypothesis relying on telemetry, when reviewed, then the corresponding event exists or is listed as a needed bead.

items.title: Write playtest protocol, consent form, surveys and observation sheet
items.description:
## Why
Telemetry must not replace direct observation; a consistent protocol makes sessions comparable.
## What
`docs/playtesting/protocol.md`: session script (setup, minimal briefing, think-aloud prompts, no-help rule, time-boxes), observer sheet (timestamped notes, "confusion/delight/wait-I-can-do-that" tags aligned with feedback tags), post-session survey (Likert items mapped to hypotheses + open questions), consent/recording form template, remote-session variant.
## Scope
- In: Protocol, templates in docs/playtesting/templates/
- Out: Recruitment (e35-recruit-testers)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the survey, when mapped to fun-hypotheses.md, then every survey-sourced hypothesis has a corresponding question.
- AC-2 [manual] Given a dry-run session with one internal tester, when completed, then the protocol fits in 60 minutes and gaps found are fixed in the doc.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the consent form, when reviewed, then it states what is recorded, how long it is kept, and how to withdraw.

items.title: Deploy playtest builds to GitHub Pages with build IDs
items.description:
## Why
Testers need a stable URL per round and bug reports must identify the exact build.
## What
CI workflow deploys the game to Pages under `/play/` (latest main) and `/play/<tag>/` for tagged playtest releases (`playtest-rN`), alongside backlog.html. Build SHA + tag shown in the title screen corner and embedded in bundles; `?debug=1` enables console on playtest builds.
## Scope
- In: Pages workflow extension (shared Pages site with backlog)
- In: Version stamping
- In: Release notes from CHANGELOG
- Out: Hosting elsewhere (itch.io mirror optional later)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given tag `playtest-r1` pushed, when the workflow runs, then `/play/playtest-r1/` serves that build and `/play/` still serves main.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given a deployed build, when loaded, then the title screen shows the tag/SHA matching the commit.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a backlog-only workflow run, when deploying, then existing `/play/` builds are preserved (no Pages artifact clobbering).

items.title: Internal playtest: is greybox combat fun with no rewards?
items.description:
## Why
Constitution: fighting a skeleton should be enjoyable even without XP or loot — test this at greybox, when it is cheapest to fix.
## What
Run 5 internal/friendly sessions of the m1 greybox fight with loot/XP disabled using the protocol; record ratings and observations; report in `docs/playtesting/reports/m1-combat.md` with recommended changes filed as beads.
## Scope
- In: Sessions, report, beads for findings
- Out: Implementing fixes
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given 5 sessions, when completed, then the report includes per-tester combat fun rating, median, and top 3 frictions with timestamps.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the median rating < 4/5, when the report is written, then it proposes specific changes as beads before m2 begins.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the report, when merged, then every finding links to a bead or is marked won't-fix with a reason.

items.title: Internal playtests proving each class fantasy in greybox
items.description:
## Why
m2 exit: each class's core verbs must feel like its fantasy before content production scales up.
## What
Per class (knight, archer, sorcerer, thief): 3 sessions on a greybox encounter with multiple routes; measure route choice, verb usage (telemetry), and fantasy rating; report `docs/playtesting/reports/m2-classes.md`.
## Scope
- In: 12 sessions, telemetry report, written findings, beads
- Out: Content (m3)
## Notes
- None.

**Integration note:** Dropped hard dependency on e34-analysis-scripts (m4); m2 sessions are analysed from exported logs by hand.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given 3 sessions per class, when completed, then each class has a fantasy rating and a list of verbs used vs available.
- AC-2 [manual] Given a class whose testers used < 50% of its core verbs unprompted, when reported, then discoverability beads are filed.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the sessions' playtest bundles, when `pnpm playtest:report` runs, then per-class ability usage charts are included in the report.

items.title: Recruit external playtesters and schedule sessions
items.description:
## Why
External players, not the team, must demonstrate the game is fun.
## What
Recruit ≥ 16 external testers (two rounds of ≥ 8) spanning genre veterans and casual players, with at least 2 using accessibility settings; screener form, scheduling, consent collection; tracking sheet (no personal data in the repo).
## Scope
- In: Screener, outreach, scheduling
- Out: Paid recruitment platforms (only if needed)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given recruitment, when complete, then ≥ 16 consenting testers are scheduled across two rounds with a mix recorded as aggregate counts only.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the repo, when checked, then no tester personal data (names, emails) is committed.
- AC-3 [manual] Given no-shows exceed 25% in a round, when detected, then backup testers are scheduled to maintain ≥ 8 sessions.

items.title: Run external playtest round 1 on the MVP build
items.description:
## Why
The first honest measurement of the fun hypotheses with players who owe us nothing.
## What
Run ≥ 8 sessions with the protocol on a tagged `playtest-r1` build; collect bundles, observer notes and surveys; produce `docs/playtesting/reports/r1.md` scoring each hypothesis.
## Scope
- In: Sessions, report with hypothesis scorecard
- Out: Triage (e35-findings-triage)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given ≥ 8 completed sessions, when the report is written, then each pre-registered hypothesis has a measured value and pass/fail.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the collected bundles, when the analysis script runs, then the report embeds its heatmap and usage sections.
- AC-3 [manual] Given a session with a crash, when reported, then its error log and bug bundle are attached to a bead.

items.title: Triage round-1 findings into prioritized beads
items.description:
## Why
Findings are worthless unless they become prioritized work before round 2.
## What
Cluster observations, survey comments and telemetry anomalies into issues; file beads with evidence links; prioritize by hypothesis impact; select the set to fix before round 2.
## Scope
- In: Triage doc section in r1 report, beads
- Out: Fixes themselves
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given the r1 report, when triaged, then every failed hypothesis has at least one linked bead with a proposed change.
- AC-2 [manual] Given the triaged beads, when prioritized, then a "before round 2" set is labelled and each has an owner/estimate.
- AC-3 [manual] Given a finding judged out of scope, when recorded, then the reason is written in the report.

items.title: Run external playtest round 2 to validate fixes
items.description:
## Why
Confirms changes improved the experience rather than just changing it.
## What
Run ≥ 8 sessions with new testers on `playtest-r2`; same protocol and analysis; report r2 with deltas vs r1 per hypothesis.
## Scope
- In: Sessions, r2 report with r1→r2 deltas
- Out: Decision (e35-mvp-go-no-go)
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given ≥ 8 sessions with testers not in round 1, when reported, then each hypothesis shows r1 value, r2 value and delta.
- AC-2 [manual] Given a hypothesis that regressed, when reported, then the likely cause is analysed and a bead filed.
- AC-3 [integration] Given r1 and r2 bundles, when the analysis script runs in comparison mode, then side-by-side charts are produced.

items.title: Record MVP go/no-go decision against fun hypotheses
items.description:
## Why
Constitution: mobile and expansion only after the MVP proves the game is fun; this is that gate.
## What
ADR `docs/adr/NNNN-mvp-go-no-go.md` applying the pre-registered go/no-go rule to r2 results: go (proceed to post-MVP: E36 etc.), iterate (another round with named changes), or pivot; lists evidence and next steps.
## Scope
- In: ADR with evidence links
- Out: Post-MVP planning itself
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given r2 results, when the ADR is written, then it applies the pre-registered rule verbatim and states the outcome.
- AC-2 [manual] Given an "iterate" outcome, when recorded, then the ADR names the hypotheses to re-test and the changes planned.
- AC-3 [manual] Given a "go" outcome, when recorded, then mw-e36 stubs are unblocked for re-planning.

items.title: Spike: mobile browser feasibility and target devices
items.description:
## Why
Mobile only after MVP validation; before committing, measure what mobile browsers can actually run.
## What
Time-box 2 days: run the MVP build on representative iOS Safari and Android Chrome devices, measure fps/memory/load on a mobile preset, identify blockers (memory limits, WASM, audio unlock, fullscreen/orientation); ADR recommending target devices and scope.
## Scope
- In: Measurements, ADR
- Out: Implementation
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given 2 iOS and 2 Android devices, when the MVP build runs, then fps, memory and load time are recorded in the ADR.
- AC-2 [manual] Given a device that crashes or fails to load, when recorded, then the cause (memory, API) is identified or marked unknown with next steps.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the ADR, when merged, then it states go/no-go for mobile and target device floor.

items.title: Design touch controls for movement, camera and class verbs
items.description:
## Why
Keyboard/mouse verbs must map to touch without losing class expressiveness.
## What
As a mobile player, I want virtual stick, camera drag and contextual verb buttons so that I can play every class on touch. Coarse placeholder — split after the feasibility spike.
## Scope
- In: Touch input adapter onto the action map, layout customization
- Out: Anything before e36-mobile-feasibility
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given touch emulation, when the virtual stick is dragged, then the player moves proportionally.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given simultaneous stick + camera drags (multi-touch), when performed, then both apply independently.
- AC-3 [manual] Given each class, when played on a phone for 10 minutes, then its core verbs are usable (rated ≥ 3/5 by testers).

items.title: Create a mobile performance preset and memory budget
items.description:
## Why
Mobile GPUs and memory limits (esp. iOS Safari) need their own budgets.
## What
Mobile preset (render scale, shadows off/low, reduced particles, texture downscale), memory budget per spike findings, added to perf suite. Coarse placeholder.
## Scope
- In: Preset, budgets, perf suite entries
- Out: Desktop presets
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the target floor device, when the combat stress scene runs on the mobile preset, then p95 frame time ≤ 33.3 ms.
- AC-2 [perf] Given iOS Safari, when played for 20 minutes, then the tab is not killed for memory (heap within the spike-defined budget).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a desktop capability profile, when presets are chosen, then the mobile preset is never auto-selected.

items.title: Redesign HUD and menus for small touch screens
items.description:
## Why
Desktop menus and dense HUDs are unusable at phone sizes with touch targets.
## What
As a mobile player, I want HUD and menus sized for touch so that I can manage inventory, books and dialogue comfortably. Coarse placeholder.
## Scope
- In: Touch-target sizing (≥ 44 px), portrait/landscape handling, safe areas
- Out: Desktop UI
## Notes
- None.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a 390×844 viewport, when each menu renders, then all interactive targets are ≥ 44×44 CSS px and nothing overflows.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given a device rotation, when it occurs, then layout adapts without losing game state.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given a notched device safe area, when the HUD renders, then no HUD element is under the notch.
